# External MCP Server Catalog - Sweep Log, October 16-31, 2026

Archive for October 16-31, 2026. Discovery passes appear newest first. The [current sweep log](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/changelog) carries the most recent passes.

Archive: [October 1-15, 2026](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/changelog-2026-10a) | [November 1-15, 2026](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/changelog-2026-11a)

## 🆕 October 31, 2026 - Night Sweep (3 New, 3 Guides)

Four hours after the afternoon pass, and the movement came from the submission window rather than the directories: **eighteen** submissions landed on chatmcp/mcpso between `#6513` at `19:06Z` and `#6530` at `03:53Z`, while mcpservers.org carried no delta and the mcp.so `recentServers` block put exactly **six** cards above the afternoon stamp. Three shipped, and two of the three answered a live endpoint with no credential at all.

- [Lazynext Accessibility Checker MCP - WCAG Audits From Chat](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/lazynext-accessibility-checker-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://checker.lazynext.com/mcp`, **keyless**, `initialize` answering **HTTP 200** in 0.19 seconds with `serverInfo` `accessibility-checker` at **1.0.0** and `tools/list` returning all **four** tools with schemas, so the surface is measured rather than quoted. `list_rules` returned **75** WCAG criteria each tagged `static` or rendered, and two rendered scans were run on our own homepage. Mobile viewport: score **46** on `score_model` `weighted-v1`, **28** issues across **12** distinct criteria, section 508 `conforms: false` against the stated basis of WCAG 2.0 AA incorporated by 36 CFR 1194 E205.4 with **5** clauses implicated (302.1, 302.2, 302.3, 302.7, 302.9), a benchmark at the **54th** percentile of **26** sites, and a persisted report at `checker.lazynext.com/report/c036dcc1-4e6`. Desktop viewport: the first call exceeded a 60-second client timeout and the retry returned in **61.1 seconds** with score **46** and **29** issues. The findings are content-level and fixable: two `wcag-2.5.3` failures where an `aria-label` replaces rather than contains the visible text, one `wcag-1.4.10` on a `<div>` with a fixed 1000px width, and seven `wcag-1.1.1` findings that are filename `alt` text. **The reason it earns a guide is that this catalogue had no accessibility entry at all**, which makes it the only tool here that answers a procurement questionnaire rather than a ranking question. **Gap recorded:** the vendor site lists API, MCP and A2A as Pro features at **$9 per month** with the free tier at 3 rendered scans a day, and yet the endpoint accepted no key and labelled both scans `plan: "free"`, so the plan gate is documented and not enforced on the MCP path; `scan_html`, `get_report` and the site crawl were not exercised, the benchmark cohort of 26 or 27 sites is unpublished, and the repository is source available rather than open source.
- [distribution.tech MCP - Book X Creator Posts From the Chat](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/distribution-tech-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP with a **keyless guest tier** at `https://app.distribution.tech/api/mcp/guest`: `initialize` **HTTP 200** in 0.34 seconds, `serverInfo` `distribution` at **1.37.0**, and **six** tools with full schemas. `guest_status` states its own limits, **60** calls per 10 minutes per client address and **3** `plan_quote_guest` calls per **7 days**, and `inventory` at `04:02:35Z` reported **1,005** approved X creators, **86** bookable now and **255** posts carrying a current price. `resolve_audience` on a described profile (a B2B AI data layer, ecommerce and SaaS operators, US) resolved three segments and narrowed the market to **792** creators, **63** bookable and **187** priced posts with `thin: false`, and that 213-creator gap between the network and one audience is the number a founder cannot get from a DM. The account surface is documented at `/docs/agents` as **22** tools and the design is the reason for the guide: a key carries a spend **mandate**, signing a plan produces a payment link inside that mandate, brands are reviewed before their agent can buy, creator names and two alternates arrive before signing, placements can be swapped before signing, and `evidence` returns per placement. **Gap recorded:** `plan_quote_guest` failed with `unavailable: The network could not be read just now. Try again.` and consumed one of the three weekly guest quotes, so no all-in price was obtained; no brand approval was sought and nothing was purchased, so `create_campaign`, `approve_plan`, `evidence` and the mandate enforcement are read rather than driven, and the creator payout split was not read.
- [GWIX MCP - Pay, Hiring and Workforce Data With Provenance](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/gwix-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://api.gwix.ai/mcp`, where the live server answered a keyless `initialize` with **HTTP 401**, JSON-RPC `-32001`, `Authentication required: sign in with OAuth or send a GWIX API key as a Bearer token`, and `/v1/mcp` returned a different 401 shape, an RFC 7807 problem body with a `request_id`, so the public API and the MCP server sit on different routers and both are closed. The vendor's keyless sample at `https://api.gwix.ai/mcp/sample` is where this pass measured: `initialize` **HTTP 200**, `tools/list` returning **27** tools in 37,580 bytes, and `get_data_status` for the US reporting `release: "2026-W41"`, `last_complete_week: "2026-04-12"` and a sample covering the US, UK and Germany at **6 months** of lag with history from `2024-10-14`, market level only. `get_pay` for SOC **47-2111** in metro `mtr_midland_tx` for 2026-Q1, the exact example the vendor publishes, returned **74** ads with pay and percentiles of **38,215 / 48,368 / 66,781 / 76,526 / 94,694** USD per year, reproducing the vendor's own published median to the dollar, which is a stronger trust signal than any marketing page. The metadata carries the machinery: 13-week quarters of whole Monday to Sunday weeks, each country's currency converted at the period average with `fx_rate` per row, and occupation codes crosswalked to US SOC 2018 with each SOC held as a separate row set and never pooled. **The slice is new here:** the hiring entries in this catalogue are job boards and recruiting pipelines, and none of them returns pay percentiles from official surveys beside job-ad medians, which is the gap that decides an offer. **Gap recorded:** `job_offer_check`, the tool closest to a decision, returned a CloudFront **504** after 30.07 seconds while the row tools answered in 0.26 seconds, so the written-analysis path is unverified; no credential exists, so the report tools, `get_account_usage` and the credit accounting were not driven; the **247**-country claim is the vendor's where the sample proves three; and the credit cost of a typical question could not be produced.

**Read and held.** mcpservers.org `/all` came back with **23** unique slugs and the counter at **18,577** against **18,402** at the afternoon read, and every slug matched an existing file in the tree, so the page carried no delta and the counter moved because the catalogue grows rather than because the newest page changed. The **six** mcp.so cards above the afternoon stamp are dispositioned as follows, so the next pass cannot read them as fresh: `corridome` (`2026-11-01T00:15:52Z`) is a US private-equity and M&A register requiring its own membership, `corridome.com` answering **200** with no keyless surface, held on access in a class the filings entries already cover; `browse-bridge` (`23:07:27Z`) shares selected Chrome tabs with an agent at `https://mcp.browsebridge.com`, held in the deepest automation slice here; `listing-698e96` (`19:17:31Z`) is Tabulya, a Russian-language spreadsheet with AI, Python and SQL, held as localised product; `coinvello` (`19:10:08Z`) is the same arrival as `#6513` below; and `myimage2life-8891ac` (`18:02:28Z`) turns a chat image into a printed product, held as consumer retail. The **eighteen** submissions between `#6513` and `#6530` were read with bodies: `Clearcote MCP` (`#6515`) is the strongest hold of the window, about **20** tools on a Chromium fork whose fingerprint is set in C++ and whose `get_cdp_endpoint` hands the same browser to Playwright, Puppeteer, browser-use or Crawl4AI, held on class with the CDP handoff recorded as the feature to test; `conductor` (`#6519`) is **23** tools each carrying a mandatory verifier that checks the result in code before the client sees it, the most interesting reliability entry of the window and developer tooling; `SKV` (`#6526`) answered a keyless `initialize` at `https://skv.network/mcp` with `serverInfo` `skv-memory` **1.30.0** and more than **20** tools including a per-turn `turn(user_message, draft)` duty, a paged constitution, a shared cube library with voting, a court for version disputes and an isolated sandbox, held for one pass because memory plus governance is rarer than plain memory and the promotion test is whether the seal and the court are enforceable rather than self-reported; `CSI MCP` (`#6517`) drives SAP2000 and ETABS on Windows only with **67 of 67** rebuilt verification examples matching published values, held on platform and vertical; `NexusBro` (`#6528`) answered keyless at `https://nexusbro.com/api/agents/mcp` with **two** tools and a free five-page audit, held on saturation against eight SEO audit entries; `Shipvo` (`#6527`) answered at `https://sim.shipvo.dev/mcp` with `serverInfo` `shipvo` **0.0.6** and needs a key for its **18** tools, developer mobile testing; `Frank` (`#6524`) returned a measured **401** at `https://api.hifrank.ai/mcp` on **14** tools of AI-moderated customer interviews, held on saturation against four research entries with the quotable-evidence question recorded; `CoinVello` (`#6513`), `ILens` (`#6514`), `Fittest` (`#6516`), `recall` (`#6518`), `Betterloop` (`#6520`), `Wordy Page` (`#6521`), `nana800` (`#6522`), `ytranscript` (`#6525`) and `VocaLingo` (`#6530`) round out the window in the agent payments, developer tooling, materials science, memory, analytics, publishing, locale, transcript and media generation classes this catalogue already carries.

**Count.** The guide tree held **1,073** server entries before this pass and holds **1,076** after it, across **1,466** files. Sources: the mcp.so homepage `recentServers` block read directly (**132** parsed cards, newest `2026-11-01T00:15:52Z`), mcpservers.org `/all` through the r.jina.ai reader proxy with `X-Return-Format: html` (**23** unique slugs, counter **18,577**), the chatmcp/mcpso issue window **#6513** to **#6530** read with bodies, a keyless `initialize`, `tools/list`, `list_rules` and two rendered `scan_url` calls on `https://checker.lazynext.com/mcp` (**200**, **4** tools, **75** rules, 12.97s mobile and 61.1s desktop), a keyless `initialize`, `tools/list`, `guest_status`, `inventory`, `resolve_audience` and one failed `plan_quote_guest` on `https://app.distribution.tech/api/mcp/guest` (**200**, **6** tools), a keyless `initialize` on `https://api.gwix.ai/mcp` (**401**) and on `/v1/mcp` (**401**), a keyless `initialize`, `tools/list`, `get_data_status` and `get_pay` on `https://api.gwix.ai/mcp/sample` (**200**, **27** tools) with one `job_offer_check` failing at a CloudFront **504**, a keyless `initialize` on `https://skv.network/mcp` and `https://sim.shipvo.dev/mcp` (**200**), a keyless `initialize` and `tools/list` on `https://nexusbro.com/api/agents/mcp` (**200**, **2** tools), a measured **401** on `https://api.hifrank.ai/mcp`, and HTTP reads on `gwix.ai`, `gwix.ai/mcp`, `gwix.ai/pricing`, `corridome.com`, `coinvello.com/ai`, `checker.lazynext.com`, `distribution.tech`, `distribution.tech/docs`, `distribution.tech/docs/agents` and `distribution.tech/pricing`, all **200**.

## 🆕 October 31, 2026 - Afternoon Sweep (3 New, 3 Guides)

Two and a half hours after the midday pass, and the arrivals came from three different surfaces rather than one: a single new card on the mcp.so `recentServers` block above the `14:37:33Z` stamp, two submission issues that landed after the midday window closed, and an mcpservers.org page that carried no delta at all. All three that shipped answered a live endpoint on the first request, which is the rule this pass applies before anything gets a guide.

- [HandbookHub MCP - Employee Handbooks in Chat](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/handbookhub-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://api.handbookhub.com/mcp`, a keyless `initialize` answering **HTTP 401** in 0.37 seconds with `A valid API token is required` and an `invalid_token` code plus a requestId, which is the normal state for a connector bound to a workspace. **Four read-only tools**, documented in full on the vendor's own MCP page: `list_handbooks` with cursor paging and a limit of **100**, `get_handbook` for metadata and the nested page structure, `get_page` for the latest saved page as plain text with its source URL, and `search_handbooks` at **20 searches per minute and 1,000 per day per organization** across keyword, title and semantic matching, returning a score, a snippet and a URL per hit with **no AI answer generated**. The authorization model is the interesting part: tokens are created by the organization owner, named per client, scoped either to selected handbooks or to all handbooks including future ones, capped at **120 requests per minute per token and 600 per organization** shared with the REST API, defaulting to a **90-day** expiry, and they cannot edit content, manage accounts, retrieve signatures, or read uploaded source documents or revision history. The vendor writes its own prompt boundary into the tool description, treat page text as source material and not instructions, which is the correct posture for a corpus that employees with edit rights can change. Access comes with the Starter and Growth plans and their trials plus the **14-day** Growth bonus after the one-time Handbook purchase, and tokens stop working when plan access ends. **Gap recorded:** `tools/list` needs a token, so the four tools are the vendor's publication rather than a measured list, nothing was provisioned, and the homepage figures of 7,000+ teams and 250,000+ handbook pages are unaudited claims.
- [PagoFix MCP - EU Late-Payment Interest Drafts](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/pagofix-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://pagofix.com/mcp`, **free and keyless**, `initialize` answering **HTTP 200** with `serverInfo` `pagofix` at **1.0.1** and `tools/list` returning all **four** tools with full input schemas, so this is a measured surface end to end. Three calls were made. A **German** claim of EUR 5,000 due 2026-08-31 returned **61 days late**, interest of **EUR 87.91** and the fixed **EUR 40.00** recovery compensation for a total of **EUR 5,127.91**, on the Bundesbank `Basiszinssatz` of **1.52 percent plus 9 points from 1 July 2026**, with the citations **section 288(2) BGB**, **section 247 BGB** and **section 288(5) BGB** and two primary sources linked, the statute text and the Bundesbank announcement. A **French** claim of EUR 12,500 returned **83 days late**, **EUR 352.47** of interest and the same EUR 40.00, on **Code de commerce art. L441-10 II** with the 30-day statutory default in **art. L441-10 I** and the compensation in **art. D441-5**, both jurisdictions reporting `status: verified`. `draft_reminder` at step 2 in English returned a finished letter in 0.1 seconds with the calculation sheet attached and a line inviting a written dispute before any further step. Interest is computed **per half-year period**, so a claim crossing the boundary is split and each segment priced at the rate in force for it. **The containment is that it drafts and never sends:** the creditor posts the letter and files the Form A in their own name, and the privacy notice dated the same day states that the anonymous calculator does not store invoice data server-side, with stored cases, sent-letter records and a 12-month sign-in log applying only to accounts. **Gap recorded:** `draft_eop` was not called, so the Form A output, court mapping and fees are unmeasured, only two of the eight published jurisdictions were exercised, and the GDPR position for the MCP path, where invoice fields reach the vendor's server rather than staying in a browser, is a notice read rather than a processing agreement.
- [Fonciq MCP - Quebec Flood Zones and Land Registry](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/fonciq-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://api.fonciq.ca/v1/mcp`, `initialize` answering **HTTP 200** with `serverInfo` `fonciq` at **1.0.0** and `tools/list` returning all **fourteen** tools. The free half is the reason to read it: `flood_zones_lookup` is **keyless**, at **30 requests per minute and 1,000 per day per IP**, and one live call at 45.4865, -73.8980 answered in 0.26 seconds with `any_zone_found: true` against the Ville de Montreal index of flood plains as a **reference layer**, dataset URL at donnees.montreal.ca, licence **CC-BY-4.0**, with the sources' freshness stamped between 13:44:31Z and 13:48:53Z that day. The payload refuses three assumptions in its own fields: the lot boundary is not evaluated because a point is not a polygon, no zone found never means outside a flood zone, and the new-generation mapping in force by sector since 1 March 2026 is not included, so every answer links the official provincial map. The paid half is the Registre foncier: lot resolution and profiles with assessment-roll values in cents, index requests, deeds and cadastral plans at **CAD 0.99 per document** excluding registry fees, batches of up to **500 lots**, and dated watches that re-check an index against a baseline snapshot. **Gap recorded:** only the free tool was called, so the thirteen registry tools, their outputs and the **0.99** price are the vendor's published position, and whether a 500-lot batch bills per lot or per job is a question for the first trial.

**Read and held.** The mcpservers.org `/all` newest page returned **22** unique slugs with the counter at **18,402** against **18,577** at the morning read, and every slug was already named in a prior disposition. Four of them read as fresh to a bare slug match and are recorded here so the next pass cannot pick them up again: `www-margoleads-io-docs-mcp` is **Margo**, `www-luriart-com` is **Luria**, `www-getpylot-com-agents` is **Pylot AI**, all three held in the October 30 evening pass, and `www-locusintel-io-docs-api` is **Locus Intel**, named in the October 30 midday pass. The rest were the catalogue's existing dispositions: `supplementscanner-mcp`, `casus-mcp`, `convertlyft-mcp`, `nextesy-mcp`, `whirrwork-com-agents`, `bibigpt-co-mcp`, `www-playfacetoface-com`, `ffxf-net-agents`, `www-gptimagehub-com-api-docs`, `sniffpup-com-docs-mcp`, `www-makeviral-ai`, `bastionhelix-com-lens-docs`, `myspainvisa-com-mcp`, `diditwork-org-agents-mcp`, `mynomadworld-com-mcp`, `zsign-io`, `diffmint-mike-tusa-workers-dev` and `globalcastai-com`. On the mcp.so side the `recentServers` block returned **140** cards where the midday read returned **30**, which is a parse variance recorded twelve hours earlier as well and not a change at the source; the only two cards above the midday stamp were `monitorbankrates`, catalogued at midday, and `handbookhub-mcp`, catalogued here. The submission window moved twice and both arrivals shipped: `#6509` Fonciq at `16:01:05Z`, which the midday pass read and did not disposition, and `#6511` PagoFix at `17:53:00Z`.

**Count.** The guide tree held **1,070** server entries before this pass and holds **1,073** after it, across **1,461** files. Sources: the mcp.so homepage `recentServers` block read directly (**140** parsed cards, newest `2026-10-31T17:06:19Z`), mcpservers.org `/all` through the r.jina.ai reader proxy with `X-Return-Format: html` (**22** unique slugs, counter **18,402**), the chatmcp/mcpso issue window **#6509** and **#6511** read with bodies in one authenticated call, a keyless `initialize` on `https://api.handbookhub.com/mcp` (**401**), a keyless `initialize` and `tools/list` on `https://pagofix.com/mcp` (**200**, **4** tools) with two `calc_claim` calls and one `draft_reminder` call, a keyless `initialize`, `tools/list` and `flood_zones_lookup` on `https://api.fonciq.ca/v1/mcp` (**200**, **14** tools), and HTTP reads on `handbookhub.com`, `handbookhub.com/mcp`, `handbookhub.com/api`, `handbookhub.com/pricing`, `pagofix.com`, `pagofix.com/privacy`, `github.com/pagofix/pagofix-mcp` and `fonciq.ca/api-gratuite/zones-inondables` all **200**.

## 🆕 October 31, 2026 - Midday Sweep (1 New, 1 Guide)

Six hours after the early morning pass, and the two directory surfaces split cleanly: the mcpservers.org newest page was entirely inside the morning dispositions, while the mcp.so `recentServers` block carried **30** cards with the newest at `2026-10-31T14:37:33Z` against `2026-10-31T03:22:19Z` at the previous read, so exactly two cards sat above the morning stamp and both were read to detail level. The issue window moved more than either: **twelve** submissions landed on chatmcp/mcpso between `#6499` at 11:19Z and `#6510` at 16:42Z, and each was dispositioned here rather than assumed.

- [MonitorBankRates MCP - Deposit and Loan Rate Benchmarks](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/monitorbankrates-mcp/) - remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.monitorbankrates.com/mcp`, **keyless**, `initialize` answering **HTTP 200** with `serverInfo` `MonitorBankRates` at **1.2.0** and `tools/list` returning all **eight** tools with their full input schemas, so the surface is measured rather than quoted. Two calls were made on the day: the national **12-month CD** average at **3.0101** percent APY as of `2026-10-31`, computed across **4,107** institutions and **9,115** quotes with `change_1w` of **+0.019**, and the **high-yield savings** average at **2.0501** percent APY across **271** institutions and **709** quotes. The dataset is every published rate at more than **8,000** banks and credit unions recomputed daily, and the eight tools read it in four directions: `get_best_rates` for one product nationally, by state or by city with local branches first, `get_average_rates` for national or state averages with the week, month and quarter change plus a daily history, `search_institutions` and `get_institution`, which return every tracked rate for one bank or credit union alongside its health letter grade, star rating and **Texas ratio**, and `get_mortgage_lenders`, which ranks lenders and brokers by home loans closed in the latest federal **HMDA** data with market share, approval share, median loan and programmes. `calculate_loan` prices the choice at today's average or a rate passed in, and the refinance mode returns monthly savings and the **breakeven in months** rather than a difference the operator has to interpret, while `get_index` serves a Housing Affordability Index where **100** means the median household exactly affords the median home at today's 30-year average, alongside Home and Auto Insurance Burden indexes with state rankings. **The reason this is a new slice rather than another finance read:** the treasury entries here read markets, macro series, Fed and Treasury public data and crypto custody, and none of them reads the **deposit side of the balance sheet at institution level**, which is where an operator's cash actually sits and the one position chosen once and reviewed rarely. Knowing the national CD average moved two basis points is a headline; knowing which institutions paying more than that would pass a Texas-ratio review is the decision. The licence string returned with every response asks for attribution and a link to the source `url`, and every row carries `as_of`, which is what makes a rate quotable at all, and the containment is that all eight tools read and calculate and nothing opens an account or moves a balance. **Gap recorded:** the vendor site answered **HTTP 403** to every request from this host including `/sitemap.xml`, behind Cloudflare, so no pricing page, coverage page or methodology note was read and the block is recorded as a bot wall rather than an absence, `change_1m` and `change_3m` came back `null` on both series although the tool documents them, and whether the keyless free surface is permanent or a launch window is stated nowhere this pass could read.

**Read and held.** `numradar` (`2026-10-31T11:35:49Z`) is the stronger of the two feed arrivals and it is held on class, not quality: a hosted WhatsApp registration check at `https://numradar.app/mcp` answering **HTTP 401** with a bearer-key challenge, priced from **9** dollars a month for 5,000 validations to **249** for 300,000, with four tools described as validate, bulk, job progress and allowance. The question it answers, whether a number can be reached on WhatsApp at all, is a real one for an outbound team choosing a channel, and it is still the verification commodity this catalogue already answers twice over with the phone intelligence entry, which returns carrier, line type, LRN, CNAM and spam reputation, and the email verification trio. What kept it out of the catalogue is evidence rather than judgement: the tool list sits behind the key, so four tools is the vendor's publication and not a measured surface, and a paid-only verification check with no keyless tier is a harder recommendation than a read that answers on the first call. The promotion test is whether registration status comes back as a quotable field per number or only as a job summary. `monitorbankrates` had itself been carried in the morning report as an undecided card, and the reason it shipped here is that the keyless surface answered, which is the rule that separates the two.

The **twelve** issue-window submissions were dispositioned as follows, each recorded so the next pass cannot read them as fresh. `mkts Market Data` (`#6505`) is strong and held on saturation: read-only quotes, fundamentals, SEC filings, screening and a point-in-time archive across **15** tools with provenance on every result, in a slice already carried by Altair, ValuEdge, fAlpha and BDE plus nine EDGAR surfaces. `Signbee` (`#6507`) sends markdown or PDF documents for two-party e-signature with SHA-256 audit trails, MIT licensed, `npx signbee-mcp` at **1.0.1** with two runtime dependencies and no hosted endpoint published, and it is a second e-signature surface beside `zsign` (`#6415`) and the lifecycle entry that already runs to signature with an audit trail. `doc2json` (`#6500`) turns a PDF, photo or text into typed JSON against a schema the caller defines, keyless for `initialize` and `tools/list` with 50 pages a month free, inside the document extraction and rendering class carried by Bannerify and url-to-pdf. `Avo Cado Read` (`#6503`) is a robots-respecting web-to-markdown reader priced per call at **0.003** USDC on Base over x402, in the reader class. `GotSOL.app` (`#6510`) is USDC payments on Solana with Privy-held keys and a **0.25** percent send fee, `Shellway Relay` (`#6499`) is a self-hosted MCP relay with auth, rate limiting and usage logs, and `web2mcp` (`#6496`) is a Cloudflare Workers gateway that turns any REST API into tools with an OpenAPI converter, all three inside the agent payments and developer infrastructure classes. `DiscoverLaunches` (`#6498`) searches new product launches read-only with three tools and is held as a thin launch directory rather than an operator data surface, `GitHubCard` (`#6501`) renders README and link-preview cards and is developer cosmetic, `The Charter Desk` (`#6506`) is live yacht charter inventory and is consumer travel, `Pokerai API` (`#6504`) is GTO poker strategy and is consumer gaming, `SlotVFX` (`#6497`) drives a desktop VFX tool for Spine and 2D games, and `AwesomeVideo` (`#6508`) does burned-in captions, dubbing and 9:16 clips in the saturated media generation class. `TradingCalc` (`#6502`) is an update request rather than an arrival, and it reports that the mcp.so submission edit form does not save, the same complaint as `#5788`, which is recorded as a platform-side defect and not acted on.

The mcpservers.org `/all` newest page came back through the r.jina.ai reader proxy with **12** unique slugs, every one of them inside the morning dispositions, `ravenwallet-pro-docs-ai`, `cymetica-com-mcp-v1-stock-vectors`, `www-reslyce-com-flow-mcp`, `yir-ai-mcp-server`, `gmapscrawl-com-google-maps-scraper-mcp`, `www-repeatpost-com-mcp`, `compi-ai`, `aiimage-com`, `reinventa-es-asistentes-ia`, `renewroster-com-docs-mcp`, `whiteboardanimation-ai-mcp` and `docs-safeprompt-dev-mcp`, so the page carried no delta. ## 🆕 October 29, 2026 - Morning Sweep (7 New, 7 Guides)

Six hours after the night pass, and this window belongs to the feeds rather than the directories. The mcpservers.org counter sat at **18,225** for the second read in a row with **90 unique slugs** across pages one to three, so no server records were added, but page one had fully rotated since the 04:00Z read and carried a different thirty cards, which is the listing re-publishing records it already holds rather than growing. The mcp.so `/feed` carried 30 cards with the newest at **2026-10-29T08:10:00Z** against `2026-10-29T03:04:38Z` at the night read, three of them new. The submission window ran **#6367 to #6377**, eleven issues in five hours, the quietest window on this tracker in weeks and almost entirely local tooling from individual maintainers. Six of the seven entries below are local servers whose package metadata carries the evidence rather than an endpoint, and the one hosted surface was verified at its authorization boundary, where the scopes decide what a business can actually do.

- [Emailit MCP - Send, Deliver and Debug Email From Chat](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/emailit-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://api.emailit.com/mcp`, answering a bare `initialize` with **HTTP 401** and `{"code":-32000,"message":"Authorization Bearer token required"}`, with `WWW-Authenticate` naming `https://api.emailit.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`. That document returns resource `https://api.emailit.com/mcp`, authorization server `https://api.emailit.com`, bearer methods supported in the header, and **two scopes, `sending` and `full`**. The vendor's documentation, updated **2 October 2026**, states **135 tools** covering the full API v2, sign-in by OAuth 2.1 with PKCE or an API key as a bearer token, an access token lasting **15 minutes** and a refresh token good for **60 days of inactivity** that rotates on every use, where reusing an old one revokes the connection. The line that earns the entry is **workspace scoping**: consent picks all workspaces or a subset, and any call may name a workspace by ID or exact name without changing the connection default, so two client accounts can be worked in two conversations at once. It sits beside `AhaSend`, which sends one message and returns a result, and covers what actually breaks: sending domains and their authentication records, audiences, campaigns and the bounce investigation that follows a customer asking why they never got it.

- [LeadSync MCP - Meta Lead Ads Into Your CRM From Chat](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/leadsync-mcp/) · local stdio from npm as `@leadsync/mcp` **0.1.1**, installed by `npx -y @leadsync/mcp` with `LEADSYNC_API_KEY` in the environment and Node 20 or later, plus a companion skills package that registers the server for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or every one of them at once and stores the key in `~/.leadsync/.env` after `login`. It connects Meta lead forms to Google Sheets, CRMs, email and SMS, maps the fields, adds autoresponders, sends test leads, and answers the question an operator actually asks, which is what happened to one specific lead. The catalogue carries ads platforms and it carries CRMs; the join between a paid lead and the record a salesperson works is its own system, and a broken field mapping and a plateaued campaign look identical from the outside. The limit is quoted rather than smoothed: **the ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude web apps only connect to hosted MCP servers with a sign-in, so they cannot use this server**, which makes it a desktop-side tool for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Gemini CLI.

- [Terebyte MCP - One Encrypted Room for an Agent](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/terebyte-mcp/) · local stdio from npm as `terebyte` **0.1.1**, Apache-2.0, installed by `npx -y terebyte mcp` on Node 22 or later. This is the least-privilege shape this catalogue has recorded for files: the member opens **one room** in an end-to-end encrypted vault to the agent, literally pairing with a **six-character code** typed into the Terebyte app under Rooms, Connect an agent, and chooses **what the agent may do and for how long**. The vendor states the boundary as the product, that the agent sees that room and nothing else, and everything is encrypted and decrypted on the computer running the server so the vendor's own servers hold sealed bytes. Inside the room it lists, reads and writes files, makes a **Sealed Link**, and uses the room's board. Against the catalogue's drive and document entries, which open a whole account until the credential is revoked, this is a consent design rather than an access-control setting, and the trade is stated honestly: a lost key is lost, because the vendor cannot recover what it cannot read.

- [Bannerify MCP - Render Templates Into Images and PDFs](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/bannerify-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://api.bannerify.co/mcp`, answering a bare `initialize` with **HTTP 401** `invalid_token, Missing bearer token`, and a protected-resource document at `https://api.bannerify.co/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` naming resource `https://api.bannerify.co/mcp`, authorization server `https://progressive-cushion-36.authkit.app`, `resource_name` **Bannerify** and documentation at `bannerify.co/docs/mcp/overview`, with the same document served at the `/mcp` suffix path. OAuth runs with dynamic client registration on a free account, so there is no key to paste. Six tools are published: `list_templates`, `get_template`, `get_project`, `create_image`, `create_pdf` and `create_image_from_shapes`, rendering PNG, JPEG, WebP or PDF in the same request. The distinction from the generation servers in this catalogue is the one that matters to a business: the template path keeps the design fixed and varies the data, so the hundredth asset matches the first, while the shape path exists only for the case where no template fits.

- [GhostPaw Email MCP - An IMAP Mailbox for an Agent](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/ghostpaw-email-mcp/) · local stdio from npm as `@ghostpaw/email` **0.5.10**, MIT, repository `GhostPawJS/email`, installed by `npx -y @ghostpaw/email mcp` on Node 24 or later, with five tools: `mail_read`, `mail_search`, `mail_compose`, `mail_organize` and `mail_sync`. The design decision recorded here is the **local SQLite cache** with threading, full-text search and folder synchronisation, because an assistant that re-reads a mailbox from the server on every question is useless above a few thousand messages, and `mail_search` can read the cache or the server while `mail_sync` reconciles the two. The engine is written with **no runtime dependencies**, which for a component that sits beside credentials is a property rather than a style choice, and the same five tools power the stdio server, the `ghostpaw-email` command line, an Agent Skill and a TypeScript library.

- [Mnemosyne MCP - Memory That Retires What It Replaced](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/mnemosyne-mcp/) · local stdio from npm as `mnemosy-ai` **2.0.0** stable (with `3.0.0-rc.2` on the `@next` tag exposing the same MCP tools), MIT, repository `28naem-del/mnemosyne`, binary `mnemosy`, on Node 22.16.0 or later. The failure this one addresses is not forgetting but remembering something that stopped being true: an **evidence-backed** SQLite store where a **correction retires the memories that depended on it** instead of sitting beside them as a newer opinion, with **exact replay and bisect** so a disagreement about what the agent knew can be settled by returning to a state rather than by argument. Recall is hybrid retrieval with cross-encoder reranking, and the local engine needs **no model API key, no database server and no Docker**, so the accumulated context of a business stays on the machine that already holds the data.

- [NexaLayer MCP - Proxy Sessions That Cap Their Spend](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/nexalayer-mcp/) · local stdio from npm as `@nexalayer/mcp` **0.2.0**, MIT, binary `nexalayer-mcp`, registry entry `io.github.NexaLayer/nexalayer`. The connector question for proxy access is not whether an agent can route a request but whether it can be trusted with the meter, and this surface names **budget guardrails** as part of its own scope beside creating and listing sessions, **soft spend caps** and **sticky exit IPs**, where the sticky half is what makes a multi-request task hold one apparent origin. Early-access launch pricing was about **$0.23 per GB** read from the live products API at submission and the vendor states it may change, so the entry records a dated observation rather than a quote. Two traps are recorded with it: a **soft cap is soft**, a guardrail the session respects rather than a provider-enforced billing ceiling, and the name collides with an unrelated `nexlayer-cloud` listing that installs as `nexlayer-mcp`, while the PyPI `nexalayer` package is an SDK and not the MCP entry point.

- [User Intuition Research MCP - Qualitative Research With Real People](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/user-intuition-research-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.userintuition.ai/mcp`, registry `ai.userintuition/research`, submission `#6308`. A bare `initialize` returned **HTTP 401 with `{"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"Missing Authorization header"}`**. The ordering is the design decision that earns the entry: the agent **plans the study first**, from a brief, before anything is recruited, so the research design is reviewable instead of implied. Then it recruits from a vetted panel of **over four million consumers** or from your own users, and runs AI-moderated **voice, chat or video** interviews of twenty to thirty minutes each in **more than eighty languages**. The limit is recorded honestly: a consumer panel answers a consumer question and answers a B2B question badly, and consistent AI moderation is a strength for comparability and a weakness the moment the conversation needs someone to break the script.

- [Mobzio MCP - Marketplace Deeplinks and Attributed Orders](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/mobzio-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://app.mobz.io/mcp`, submission `#6302`, docs at `app.mobz.io/docs/mcp`. It answered **HTTP 401** without a token, and the neighbouring `/api/mcp` answered **403**, so the documented route is the real one. Deeplinks for **Wildberries, Ozon, Yandex Market and Kaspi** with daily **click statistics per link**, orders **attributed to each link with amounts**, a daily account overview, link diagnosis and link creation. **Eight read tools and one write tool, and nothing can be deleted**, which is the right default for an attribution ledger and a constraint to know before planning cleanup. Tool descriptions are English and the returned data is **Russian**. The honest limit is that attribution is link-level, not person-level: it answers which link produced an order, not which customer touched which other link first. This is the Russian and CIS seller set rather than the Amazon and Etsy set the rest of the catalogue assumes.

- [Pandus MCP - WCAG 2.2 Accessibility for Commerce Sites](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/pandus-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://pandus.online/mcp`, found on the mcpservers.org `/all` page. A bare `initialize` returned **HTTP 200** with **three tools keyless** (`search_rules`, `explain_rule`, `explain_wcag_criterion`), and the vendor documents **ten** with seven behind sign-in or a token, plus two prompts. The part that matters for an operator is not the finding but the fix: every rule card carries what is wrong, **who is affected**, and how to fix it **in code and on Shopify, WooCommerce, PrestaShop and Shoptet**, so the agent can find the template that renders the problem and then re-run `start_check` and read `compare_checks` to see what was fixed, what is new and what is still open between the two latest checks. The European Accessibility Act and the ADA both make this a legal exposure question rather than a quality one. The vendor states the boundary in its own words, **automated check, not a full audit, not legal advice**, and the entry repeats it rather than softening it: axe-core derived tooling catches a fraction of real WCAG failures and misses the ones that need a person.

A bare `initialize` returns **HTTP 401** with a Portuguese body naming the header it wants, the correct shape for a fiscal system, so the surface is the vendor's published table of **36 tools**. **The draft is the reason to catalogue it**: `create_note_draft` builds the NFS-e or NFC-e, validates it exactly as the issuance path would, and leaves it in `pending_approval` with an approval link and a preview PDF carrying no fiscal value, **even when the account lock is off**, expiring after seven days, and a rejected draft returns `rejection_reason` so it can be rebuilt. Around that: `preview_nfse` validates against the official layout or the municipal provider and computes IBS and CBS before anything is transmitted, `issue_nfse` waits about twenty-five seconds for authorized, rejected, blocked or pending, correction runs by substitution (`get_substitution_draft` then `substitute_document` pointing at the original) rather than deletion, `lookup_cnpj` pulls the Receita record and reports whether the municipality uses the national system, `search_service_codes` resolves the LC 116 `cTribNac` and NBS codes, `import_invoice` reads an XML the company already issued and completes registrations, regime and numbering from it, `upload_certificate` takes the A1 certificate and `create_onboarding_link` makes the company owner supply it, `create_export` builds a per-company and per-month zip plus a spreadsheet carrying the fiscal key on a one-hour signed URL with seven-day retention, and share links are read-only with expiry and revocation. Limitations recorded: Brazil only with Portuguese tool text and rejections, setup needs an A1 certificate and municipal credentials that `how_to_get` documents rather than fetches, the repository is a manifest with the product code private, and no call was executed because the endpoint refuses everything without a key. Catalogued because the approval step is a default rather than a policy, which is the only version of it that survives an agent having a bad minute.

- [bokio-mcp - Read Your Books Without Writing Them](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/bokio-mcp/) · local stdio through `npx -y bokio-mcp`, npm `bokio-mcp` **0.5.0**, MIT, Node 22 or later, repository `diblaze/bokio-mcp` pushed `2026-10-27T22:12:08Z`, authenticated with `BOKIO_TOKEN` and `BOKIO_COMPANY_ID`, filed as submission `#6248`. **Sixty tools, of which 36 are read-only and 24 are not registered at all unless `BOKIO_ALLOW_WRITES=1`**, so the write path is absent from the tool list rather than gated inside a call and no prompt can restore it. **The arithmetic is the second half**: computed tools run over the SIE export and return finished figures in whole öre for balances at a date, a ledger for one account, VAT and profit and loss for a period, open items, **suspected double bookings** and a bank statement reconciliation, so the same question returns the same number instead of a freshly reasoned one. Read surface: journal entries, invoices, credit notes, customers, suppliers, supplier invoices, items, uploads, bank payments (read only), chart of accounts, fiscal years and the SIE export. Limitations recorded: Sweden only, no hosted endpoint so a browser client cannot attach it, one company per instance with the token in the environment, Bokio's 5,000 requests per company per month and 200 per minute, one star and first publication this week, and no call executed because the server needs a Bokio token to start. Catalogued because the four questions a founder actually asks are aggregates that a model answers badly and a computed tool answers exactly.

- [Recued MCP - One Gate Between Agents and Your Accounts](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/recued-mcp/) · self-hosted server plus web client, AGPL-3.0, install by one script, MCP on `http://127.0.0.1:7717/mcp` or a public name, per-agent contract key issued from the web app, repository `recued/recued` pushed `2026-10-27T17:54:34Z`, filed as submission `#6266`. It sits between agents and mail, calendar, files, contacts and CRM records, and **each agent connects through a contract that lists the tools it may use**: reads run immediately, writes and deletes wait for the owner's approval by default, and every call is recorded at that one gate, so the permission lives on a server the agent does not control rather than in a system prompt an injection can argue with. Before the model sees warehouse data a PII alias step replaces names, emails, organisations, phones and addresses with stand-ins while keeping the region and which people belong to the same organisation, encryption at rest uses a 24-word recovery key only the owner holds, a local copy of mail, contacts and CRM keeps reads fast, and no third party takes a cut or pipes the data. The scope statement is honest and worth quoting: not a coding agent, not a chat app, not a runner for `SKILL.md` files, and not built for long multi-step questions. Limitations recorded: the owner runs the server, holds backups and holds the key, AGPL-3.0 matters to anyone embedding it, approval fatigue is the real failure mode so the contract has to stay narrow, PII aliasing is best effort in the vendor's words, one star, and no call executed because the endpoint only exists on an installed instance. Catalogued because a gate outside the agent is the only control that survives a prompt.

- [Metis Check MCP - Signed Proof a Citation Resolves](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/metis-check-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.metisfoundry.com/mcp`, **OAuth** with a customer account and a verification permission, by Metis Foundry. An hour after the midday pass, so breadth was skipped and the work went to the three surfaces that move at this gap. mcp.so `/feed` page one came back with the same newest card, `2026-10-27T16:33:59Z`, and the same thirty cards, so nothing arrived there. mcpservers.org `/all` came back with the same newest slugs the midday pass had dispositioned. The submission window advanced by one, `#6243` at `17:53:46Z`, and re-reading the feed names against the catalog with the vendor suffix stripped turned up one name that was never ledgered, which the midday pass had not named in its report. Both finds were driven, not just described: one answered a full `tools/list` and four `tools/call` executions with no key, the other answered `tools/list` and three executions with no key.

- [TradingAgentStack MCP - Who Places the Order](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/tradingagentstack-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://tradingagentstack.com/api/mcp`, **no auth at all**, read-only, no trading account touched, by intoApex (tradingagentstack.com), MIT on the server and CC BY 4.0 on the data. Filed as submission `#6243` at `17:53Z`, the only issue after the midday window closed at `#6242`. **Driven end to end without a key**: `initialize` returned HTTP 200 as `tradingagentstack` 0.5.0 on protocol 2025-06-18, and `tools/list` returned **eight tools against the five the submission documents**, the three undocumented ones being `get_risk`, `get_incidents` and `check`, which are the three that carry the trust argument. Four calls executed: `list_category` returned an error string plus **19 categories holding 143 tools**, led by broker MCP servers and AI trading bot platforms at fourteen each, market data APIs at ten, and market data servers, risk tools, prediction markets and AI research copilots at nine each; `broker_order_gating` grouped all **fourteen official broker MCP servers by who places the order**, with six in the group where the AI trades directly (Alpaca 68 percent, Longbridge 68, NinjaTrader beta 58, moomoo 58, Tradier 50, Public 28 partial) and the vendor's own source URL plus a `last_checked` date on every row; `get_incidents` since January 2026 returned **eleven entries each tied to an official disclosure**, including Foundation's phishing sent from its own domains after a self-hosted application vulnerability and Keystone's third-party monitoring tool exposure that took 25,964 buyer records, 12,873 unpaid checkout records and the WebAuth key used to check device authenticity; and `search_tools` with `can_trade_live: true` returned twenty matches ordered by safety score, CCXT highest at 85 percent because it serves public data until trading is enabled per account. Limitations recorded: rule-based scores over custody and approval facts rather than audits, trading only with no coverage beyond that vertical, `last_checked` no fresher than 2026-10-26 on the rows read, and a curated 143 rather than a crawl, so a missing tool proves nothing. Catalogued because it answers the question about the server rather than about the money, which is the one a policy is written on.
- [Postbye MCP - How to Cancel Any Subscription](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/postbye-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://postbye.com/mcp`, **no auth at all**, read-only, by Postbye (postbye.com), carried on the feed since `2026-10-27T07:26:04Z` and never ledgered. **Driven end to end without a key**: `initialize` returned HTTP 200 as `postbye` 1.2.0 on protocol 2025-06-18, and `tools/list` returned four tools (`search_companies`, `get_cancellation_guide`, `get_cancellation_letter`, `list_categories`). `list_categories` returned **30 categories with the guide count and the number verified by hand in each**: News and magazines 863, Insurance and protection plans 714, **Software and apps 584 of which 109 are hand verified**, Streaming and entertainment 454, Phone and internet 420, Finance and credit 419, against a tagline claim of 8,600+ companies. Three searches against the software category: `hubspot` returned one match cancellable **by mailed letter only**, `adobe` returned five including separate entries for Acrobat and Lightroom with each plan cancelled separately, and `quickbooks` returned QuickBooks Online with the full click path through the Intuit Account Manager plus the note that an App Store or Play Store purchase is cancelled there instead. `get_cancellation_guide` for hubspot returned two mailing addresses on file (2 Canal Park, Cambridge MA 02141 as primary, plus a Sydney address), the certified-mail option, and three pre-cancellation checks, **labelled honestly as general points for any software subscription rather than rules lifted from HubSpot's pages**. One schema correction worth the entry: `get_cancellation_guide` requires `slug` and answers `Missing required argument: slug` with `isError: true` when sent a company name, so the search has to run first. Limitations recorded: the dataset is dated by month rather than checked per page (the HubSpot guide said April 2026), only 109 of 584 software guides carry hand verification, the pre-cancellation checks are class-level and not contract-level, and coverage is consumer-weighted so a niche B2B vendor can be absent. **Also identified this cycle (not catalogued):** `singapore-proxy` on the feed, a real Singapore mobile IP through physical Singtel and M1 SIMs for agents that need to fetch geo-locked pages or run Singapore-localised searches, held as **developer proxy infrastructure rather than an operator record** and already covered in class by the proxy tooling on the listing. `how.is`, which the same feed-name sweep flagged, was found to be **already catalogued on October 25** with a full guide, and the probe was re-run to confirm it is still live (`initialize` 200 as `how.is` 1.0.0, seventeen tools, the `domain_trust` sample answering `likely_safe` with a zero-charge receipt) so nothing new was written. `drop.media` (media library across agents, HTTP 401 at `https://drop.media/mcp`), `cardboard-ai` (chat-driven video editor, 308 at `cardboard.ai/mcp`), `lorekeeper`, `testwell-lab-tests`, `ask-a-human-expert`, `trulata`, `relaylink`, `pidgeon`, `agent-inbox`, `blaze`, `pixelflow`, `promptwise`, `mythex`, `xhostd` and `aoci-code` all carry dispositions from the October 27 midday and October 26 passes and were not re-read; each was confirmed present in the ledger this cycle so none can be read as fresh by the next pass.

## 🆕 October 27, 2026 - Midday Sweep (6 New, 6 Guides)

Nearly nine hours after the night pass the listing had moved by seven, 17,714 to 17,721, the smallest move measured on this surface all week, and page one had rotated again, so breadth cost three fetches and the weight went to the two surfaces that do move at this gap: the feed, which carried seven cards after the night cutoff, and the submission window, which advanced from `#6214` to `#6242` with twenty-seven issues and no `#6237`. Four of the six finds answer `initialize` with a refusal that states its own terms, two answer with the whole tool surface open and no key at all, and one pair completes a comparison the night pass named and deferred rather than half-documented.

- [FlipProfit MCP - Marketplace Fees to the Cent](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/fliprofit-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.fliprofit.com/mcp`, **no auth at all**, read-only, GET only upstream with CORS open, by FlipProfit (fliprofit.com). **Driven end to end without a key**: `initialize` returned HTTP 200 as `fliprofit-mcp` 1.2.0, `tools/list` returned three tools (`calculate_fees`, `compare_platforms`, `get_fee_changes`), and `compare_platforms` was executed against live rates for a $50 sale with a $10 item cost and $7.50 shipping, returning **thirteen platforms ranked by profit**: Vinted $32.50 on no fee, Depop $30.40, TikTok Shop $29.50, Reverb $27.91, Mercari and Facebook Marketplace $27.50, Etsy $27.30, Grailed $27.26, Whatnot $26.75, TCGplayer $25.57, eBay $25.30, Amazon $24.01 and Poshmark $22.50, each with its calculator link. **The distinction this entry exists to make** is that a resale marketplace and a storefront price the same item against different schedules, and the delta between the best and worst platform here is 44 percent of the profit on an identical sale. Beyond the arithmetic, `get_fee_changes` returns dated fee changes each with the platform's own source URL and the date FlipProfit last verified it, published also as an Atom feed, and every 4xx and 5xx is RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable code. Documented upstream surface read alongside: OpenAPI 3.1, `/api/v1/fees/<platform>`, `/api/v1/compare`, `/api/v1/fees` for valid options and an `llms.txt`. Limitations recorded: US rates in USD only, `compare_platforms` uses each platform's default options so a category or seller tier has to be passed on `calculate_fees` before a margin is quoted, fee rules in force on a past date and change reminders sit behind Fee Watch at $6 a month or $60 a year with a 600 request per minute key, and the vendor key list documents twelve platforms while the live tool description carries thirteen with Vinted reachable. Catalogued as the item the night pass named first for this cycle, and because the alternative is a model computing marketplace fees from memory.

- [Seller Profit Doctor MCP - Storefront Profit Math](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/seller-profit-doctor-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://sellerprofitdoctor.com/api/mcp` with SSE responses, **no auth and no sign-in on the free tools**, registry `com.sellerprofitdoctor/free-tools`, by Seller Profit Doctor. `initialize` returned HTTP 200 as `sellerprofitdoctor-free-tools` 1.5.0 and `tools/list` returned **sixteen tools**, one more than the vendor page documents, across Etsy, Shopify and Amazon: `sellerprofit_checkup` returning a grade word with level 1 to 5, `sellerprofit_etsy_fees` and `sellerprofit_etsy_profit` line by line including payment processing charged on tax and the Offsite Ads cut, `sellerprofit_offsite_ads`, `sellerprofit_shipping_gap`, `sellerprofit_ads_breakeven`, `sellerprofit_price_for_margin`, `sellerprofit_sale_breakeven` for how many extra orders a discount needs to hold the same monthly profit, `sellerprofit_compare_fees` across all three platforms, `sellerprofit_ads_roas_breakeven`, `sellerprofit_box_billing` on dimensional weight, `sellerprofit_shopify_plan_fit`, `sellerprofit_shopify_order_fees`, `sellerprofit_amazon_fees`, `sellerprofit_amazon_ads_breakeven` and `sellerprofit_rates` for the fee table the numbers use. **The containment is the honesty of the output**: every result lists the defaults it filled in, Amazon fulfilment, storage and returns carry `estimate: true` and sit outside the loss total because Amazon measures size and stock, a check-up with too few answers returns no grade and a `grade.missing` list instead of inventing one, and each fixture's dollar value is scoped to the condition that orders hold. Paired here with FlipProfit because they answer different questions: storefront economics against resale economics, and the second question, whether the ad spend, the discount and the box size leave anything behind. Limitations recorded: US rates, Etsy is the default platform so `platform` must be set for Shopify or Amazon, the paid full-report surface is a separate endpoint so a free-wired assistant cannot run up a bill, and the Offsite Ads share defaults to 10 percent, the figure Etsy gave at launch in 2020, flagged as a default when the seller does not know it.

- [SpendQuery MCP - Federal Contract Data for Agents](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/spendquery-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://api.spendquery.com/mcp`, **no auth and no sign-in**, read-only, by SpendQuery (spendquery.com). `initialize` returned HTTP 200 advertising tools, prompts and resources with instructions that are a method rather than a pitch (call `get_catalog` once for metrics, dimensions, the QueryPlan schema and worked examples, then write the plan), and `tools/list` returned **thirteen tools** against the twelve named in the vendor's `llms.txt`: `get_catalog`, `run_plan`, `search_codes`, `search_recipients`, `browse_codes`, `get_notice`, `size_standard`, `naics_finder`, `vehicle_match`, `search_far`, `get_far_section`, `search_local_bids` and `sbir_awards`. **`run_plan` is the reason to catalogue it**: the answer returns with status `ok`, `clarify`, `unsupported` or `error`, a one-paragraph answer, the query and the SQL, so a figure can be re-run and checked instead of accepted, and an out-of-coverage question is declined rather than guessed. Data read from the vendor pages: USAspending.gov prime awards FY2023 through FY2026 dated through Sep 30, 2026, open SAM.gov contract notices, the FAR and DFARS as codified in the eCFR, SBA size standards under 13 CFR 121.201, SBIR and STTR awards since 1983, and state, county and city bids where those governments publish them as open data, most sources refreshing daily with the as-of date shown. The line that matters for an operator is stated in the server's own instructions: **amounts are obligations, money committed, not outlays**. Limitations recorded: subawards and non-publishing local governments are absent, award data lags filing, a SAM.gov notice answers about an opportunity and not about the contract that follows it, and bid strategy is outside the surface.

- [BugHerd MCP - Client Feedback Inside the Editor](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/bugherd-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.bugherd.com/mcp`, **OAuth**, the official server by BugHerd (bugherd.com). `initialize` without a token returned HTTP 401, which is the correct shape for an account-gated server, so the surface comes from the vendor's published tool names and setup articles: `get_task_details`, `list_project_tasks`, `list_my_tasks`, `list_all_tasks`, `update_task` for status, assignee, priority, severity and due date, `add_comment` into the task thread, `create_task`, `create_project` and `update_project`. What travels with each task is the finding: the screenshot or screen recording, the URL, the CSS selector, the client comment, the attachments and the technical details captured when the client clicked, plus console output and replay where the plan includes them. **The risk is named rather than smoothed over**, because `add_comment` writes to a surface a paying client reads, so an agent posting "fixed, redeployed" before the deploy is live has told the client something untrue in the thread they watch; the vendor's own framing, that the human reviews what was done on the board or in the thread, is recorded here as the correct default. Containment recorded: the permission set mirrors the connecting user's existing BugHerd permissions, the organization chosen at connect time bounds what the client can reach, and connected clients can be reviewed and revoked, all of which make client separation a property of the connection rather than of a prompt. Clients named by the vendor: Claude Code, Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, VS Code with Copilot, Windsurf, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Zed and Onyx. Limitations recorded: no tool was executed because every path needs an account, what the client attached reaches the assistant recordings included, console and replay depend on the plan and the site integration, and BugHerd reports what a person saw rather than what is broken.

- [byondr Receipts MCP - Receipts to Checked CSV](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/byondr-receipts-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://byondr.co/receipts/mcp`, **no auth at all** on the free surface, registry `co.byondr/receipts`, by byondr (byondr.co). **Driven without a key**: `initialize` returned HTTP 200 as "Receipts & invoices to spreadsheet" 0.1.0 and `tools/list` returned two tools with complete schemas: `extract_documents` taking `files`, `country`, `currency`, `date_order`, `exports`, `quickbooks_currency` and `quickbooks_date_format`, and `create_upload` taking `bytes` and `filename` and returning a one-hour signed URL for anything over 2 MB up to 100 MB. The differentiator over a form is the field state: vendor, date, currency, line items, tax and total each come back `ok`, `check` or `missing`, doubtful documents are flagged with the reason instead of guessed, and a receipt already submitted is marked as a duplicate. Exports are CSV, line-item CSV, QuickBooks CSV or a zip of the originals renamed by date, vendor and total, and the QuickBooks-specific currency and date-format inputs are the tell that this was built for an import that either parses or fails. Retention recorded because it is the shortest in this catalog for a document service: files are deleted after 24 hours and never used for training. Limits recorded: 25 documents per call, 10 MB per file, PDFs up to 10 pages, two tools only with no list or query, and the server is at 0.1.0 so the shape may move.

- [WatchCron MCP - Know When a Job Stops Reporting](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/watchcron-mcp/) · local stdio through `npx -y watchcron-mcp`, published on npm as `watchcron-mcp` 1.0.0 with a `watchcron-mcp` bin and the repository `watchcron/watchcron-mcp`, authenticated with `WATCHCRON_API_KEY`, by WatchCron (watchcron.com). No endpoint to probe, and that is recorded rather than worked around: `mcp.watchcron.com` does not resolve and `watchcron.com/mcp` refuses a POST with HTTP 405, so the evidence is the package and its README, which documents **nine tools**: `list_monitors` with a tag filter, `get_monitor`, `create_monitor` from an interval or a cron expression **returning the ping URL to add to the job**, `update_monitor` for schedule, grace period and tags, `pause_monitor`, `delete_monitor`, `get_pings`, `get_incidents` and `list_channels`. **The model is a dead man's switch**, which is the only monitoring shape that catches a job that fails silently: the job sends one HTTP request when it finishes and silence past the grace period is the alert, so nothing has to expose a port or install an agent, and curl or wget is enough. Alert routing read from the vendor site: email, Slack, Discord, Google Chat, Matrix, Mattermost, ntfy, Opsgenie, PagerDuty, RocketChat, SMS and webhook, on the same account as uptime, domain and SSL expiry, port, blocklist and cloud cron monitors. Risks recorded as rules rather than warnings: a monitor that never receives a ping reads healthy, a grace period tighter than the job's real runtime pages until the team stops reading the pages, `delete_monitor` is permanent and takes the history with it, and the API key is an operational credential that can create, pause and delete monitors. Catalogued because the jobs an operator actually needs watched are the ones nobody looks at, and because the ping-URL pattern is the version of this that gets wired up.

- [Reachkit MCP - Cold Email Campaigns an Assistant Can Run](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/reachkit-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://reachkit.ai/mcp`, registry `ai.reachkit/reachkit` 1.0.0, by Reachkit. `initialize` returned HTTP 401 `{"error":"unauthorized"}` with no challenge header, so the contract came from the two discovery documents: `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` returned 200 with one resource, its own authorization server, header bearer tokens and `scopes_supported: ["mcp"]`; `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` returned 200 with an **RFC 7591 registration endpoint** at `/oauth/register`, `token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported: ["none"]` for a public client, PKCE `S256` only, authorization code and refresh grants, a userinfo endpoint and identity claims `sub`, `email`, `email_verified`. Vendor-documented surface in six flows: search 500M+ people and 70M+ companies by title, seniority, industry, location, size and technology, import contacts with verified work emails at one credit each with a refund when no verified email is found, research a list row by row into merge-tag columns, write sequences with A/B variants, merge tags and spintax plus a preview of every email as it sends, attach inboxes and schedule, pause and read analytics, and list, label and answer Unibox conversations. **The spending path is sending reputation rather than money**: a launched campaign goes out from inboxes attached to the operator's domains, and the vendor keeps the approval step in the client's behaviour while the token carries a single `mcp` scope, which is the honest arrangement recorded here rather than a scope-level containment. Catalogued because cold outreach is the one acquisition channel where every step is mechanical and the handoffs are where campaigns die. Held details: reply handling needs the Scale plan, and one scope means an agent that reads analytics can also launch.

Auth is a static bearer token with no OAuth at all, in three forms - header, `/t/<token>` path segment or `?token=` query - with the header taking precedence, an anonymous `anon_` token minting free at 600 calls an hour and 30 day retention, and Pro tokens verifying offline with Ed25519 at 6000 calls an hour. Containment recorded: local servers keep every record on the machine, the README states a bare hosted endpoint can initialize and list tools but does not authorize tool calls, and money arithmetic is computed to the minor unit rather than estimated. - [Veyra MCP - Spend Limits for an Agent That Can Pay](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/veyra-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://veyra.money/api/mcp`, registry `io.github.zapxlabs/veyra` 0.1.0, non-custodial USDC on Base. This is the rare remote endpoint that answers more than it refuses: `initialize` returned HTTP 200 as server `veyra` 0.1.0 on protocol `2025-06-18`, `tools/list` returned 200 with seven tools (`get_capabilities`, `get_budget`, `list_payment_sources`, `create_payment`, `get_payment`, `list_payments`, `cancel_payment`), and only `tools/call` returned 401 `MISSING_CREDENTIAL`, so the schema is public and the account is not. **The containment model is the reason it is catalogued**, and the vendor states its own limits plainly: limits must stay consistent (auto-approve at or below ask, ask at or below per-payment, per-payment at or below daily) and a policy that violates that is rejected at edit time with a reason; payments under auto-max proceed with no prompt, the ask band returns `awaiting_approval` with a one-time link that lapses after 24 hours, and anything over the ask band or the daily cap is blocked server-side. Auto-pay works through a capped ERC-20 `approve` to a relayer the vendor operates, and the documentation is blunt that the token contract caps **how much** the relayer may move but not **who** it may move funds to, which is the policy engine, with the recipient allowlist as the only control on destination. Also recorded: a simulated rail that returns `confirmed_simulated` with `simulated: true` and is labelled in the API, the dashboard and the tool description so it can never be reported as a real payment, an audit log of 7 days on Free and 90 on Pro and a year on Team with the events that widen authority named (`source.allowance_granted`, `agent.policy_updated` with limits before and after, `agent.credential_rotated`), and USDC on Base only so policy limits stay exact without a price feed. Held to no money being moved in this pass: no payment was created, and the approval page is authenticated by possession of the token plus the matching wallet rather than by a login.

Containment recorded: DMs go out through Meta's **official Instagram API** on a connected Business or Creator account and the agent never logs in to Instagram, only commenters receive the DM, and the tool descriptions and the bundled Agent Skill instruct the agent to show the keyword, the DM and the target and wait for approval. **Recorded because it corrects a claim this catalog is careful about**: as of October 2026 Meta publishes an official MCP server for ads and not for organic posts, comments or DMs, so every Instagram MCP server is third-party and this one is a third-party platform on Meta's official API rather than a scraper.
