## 🆕 October 26, 2026 - Late Sweep (5 New, 5 Guides)

Eleven hours after the midday pass the listing had moved by three, 17,522 to 17,525, with page one in the identical order, so breadth was repetition and the pass spent its weight where a delta lands at this gap: the submission window, which advanced from `#6176` to `#6196` with no gaps, the feed, which rotated cards in at the top, and the endpoints themselves. Four of the five finds answer `initialize` with HTTP 401, which made the discovery documents the primary evidence: a protected-resource document names the resource and the scopes an agent can hold, an authorization-server document states whether a client can register itself and whether PKCE is mandatory, and the difference between a server publishing six separate scopes and one publishing a single coarse scope is visible before anyone signs in.

- [PickFu MCP - Consumer Research Panels an Assistant Can Run](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/pickfu-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.pickfu.com/mcp`, OAuth behind WorkOS with a device-code grant, registry `com.pickfu/mcp` 1.0.0, by PickFu (pickfu.com). `initialize` returned HTTP 401 `authentication_required` with a `resource_metadata` pointer **in the body**, so the contract was read from two documents: the protected-resource response names the resource, one authorization server, header bearer tokens, identity scopes only (`openid`, `email`, `profile`, `offline_access`) and a WorkOS `jwks_uri`; the authorization-server response names authorize, **device authorization** and introspection endpoints on `auth.pickfu.com`, `client_id_metadata_document_supported: true`, PKCE `S256` and grants for authorization code, refresh token and device code. Vendor-documented surface: `save_survey` with create, update and template-draft modes, `publish_survey`, `stop_survey` with unused responses refunded, `delete_survey`, `get_survey` with questions, options, AI summaries and a per-question results object carrying vote totals and the winner, `get_survey_responses` paginated with explanations, demographics, stored translations and van Westendorp price answers, `add_respondents`, `rate_response` and `pin_response` for panel quality, `export_survey_results` in CSV, PDF and PNG with short-lived signed CSV links, `list_available_targeting` and `list_available_reporting`, `build_poll_url`, template and tag tools, an upload session for local files (a browser link, a `pfuh_` token and an expiry about fifteen minutes out), `generate_image` with MCP Apps inline cards, and a feature-gated synthetic-audience set that must not be submitted without explicit approval and must not be mixed with human results. **The money path is why it is catalogued**: `publish_survey` spends the account's credit balance and then charges the saved card, returning HTTP 402 only when no usable card exists, and the documented flow keeps the poll an unpublished draft, prices it against question types, sample size and targeting, and waits for approval before that call - preview, price, approve, then spend. Limitations recorded: no tool was executed because every path needs an account, the approval gate lives in client behaviour rather than in scope, multi-question surveys are priced per question and an added open-ended "why" question wastes a slot because an explanation is already mandatory on every response, synthetic audiences are beta and feature-gated, `mine: true` on `list_surveys` requires OAuth so the two credential paths are not equal, and a preference result is not demand. Catalogued because the consumer-research class was empty in this catalog and because a validated name, package or price is the most expensive thing a small brand gets wrong.
- [AXL MCP - Courses, CRM, Checkout and Email Behind One Agent Surface](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/axl-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://app.axl.tech/mcp`, stateless and POST-only, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE, no registry entry found, by AXL EdTech Booster, LLC (axl.tech). A GET answered with the clearest refusal read this cycle: HTTP 405 and `this MCP server is stateless - it exposes no GET SSE stream and no DELETE session termination. Send JSON-RPC over POST.` `initialize` without a token returned 401. The protected-resource document publishes `scopes_supported: ["mcp"]`; the authorization-server document publishes a **registration endpoint** at `/oauth/register` (an RFC 7591 public client), `token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported: ["none"]`, PKCE `S256`, authorization code and refresh grants and a revocation endpoint. Vendor-stated surface: roughly 1,100 account operations behind a small fixed tool set the agent navigates itself - courses and LMS with lessons, hosted video, auto-graded tests and certificates; webinars; community; appointments and paid sessions; landing pages, checkout, order bumps and subscriptions; CRM and pipelines; nine-channel messaging; email campaigns; voice and chat agents; analytics and attribution - and a successful write returns a link to the created record in the admin. **The containment is the finding**: 21 sensitive operations are removed from the AI surface in the server rather than filtered in a prompt (billing writes, token minting, permission changes, admin creation), the OAuth token is an ordinary admin token under one coarse scope that carries per-field rights, the documented route to a narrower connection is an API key with read rights only, HTML writes refuse until the agent echoes a guide token, and publishing and sending stay separate actions. Limits read from its own documentation: concurrency rather than rate limiting with 429 and `Retry-After` plus an `X-Concurrency-Limit` header to read rather than a hard-coded number, uploads that leave the MCP surface for one raw PUT so an MCP-only agent cannot finish one, long responses truncated near 200,000 characters, and a billing-blocked account answering everything except billing reads with 403 `lockedSchoolAccessDenied`. Limitations recorded: no tool call was executed, the operation count is the vendor's own, and stateless transport means a client requiring an SSE stream needs a bridge such as `mcp-remote`.
- [Customermates MCP - An Open-Source CRM an Assistant Can Operate](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/customermates-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://customermates.com/api/v1/mcp` with per-workspace URLs at `/api/v1/mcp/w/<WORKSPACE_ID>`, OAuth or a 64-character `x-api-key`, registry `io.github.benjiwagner/customermates`, core AGPL-3.0 and self-hostable with Docker Compose, by Customermates (customermates.com). `initialize` returned HTTP 401 `{"error":"unauthorized"}`; the protected-resource document answers with `jwks_uri` on its own host, RS256 resource signing and identity scopes. **This is the first entry in this catalog's thin CRM class whose core is open source**, which removes the vendor from the data path while keeping the same endpoint. The permission model is why it earns a guide: every operation runs inside exactly one workspace, a workspace URL accepts only its own credentials, and the failures are named rather than generic - 406 without the `Accept` header, 403 `workspace_mismatch` for another workspace's key, 403 `insufficient_permissions` when the user's role lacks `Read access All` on the API and Webhooks row, 403 `plan_required` for a cloud workspace awaiting its first plan, and a `resource_metadata` pointer on a wrong-workspace token so the client re-authorizes instead of silently writing. The reference reads as a full CRM rather than a reader: `get_workspace_context` returning user, company, roles, connected accounts and Knowledge Base in one call, `discover_record_types`, `query_crm_records`, `search_crm_records`, `read_crm_record`, `mutate_crm_record`, `preview_crm_deletion`, import and export, `query_crm_measure`, messaging and `send_email` with save and discard drafts, calendars, routines, Knowledge Base pages, roles, teams, webhooks and trash, plus LinkedIn sales lookups. `?toolsets=` narrows the surface to records, messaging or workspace. Limitations recorded: no per-key scoping, so a key carries its creator's permissions in full and the narrow instrument is the toolset parameter; the server's confirmation guidance before deleting or sending is explicitly **not** enforced by the server; messaging, calendar and social tools need a cloud plan at Pro or higher; and no tool call was executed, so names come from the vendor reference rather than a live `tools/list`.
- [Rus.sh MCP - Short Links, QR Codes and Click Analytics in the Assistant](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/rus-sh-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://rus.sh/mcp`, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE or an API key as a bearer token, registry `sh.rus/mcp` 1.0.0, works on every plan including Free, by Sweent (rus.sh). `initialize` returned 401, and the authorization-server document is the most granular small surface read this cycle: **six scopes split by object and by verb** - `account:read`, `links:read`, `links:write`, `analytics:read`, `qr:read`, `qr:write` - with a registration endpoint, PKCE `S256`, `protected_resources: ["https://rus.sh/mcp"]` and a public client. Sixteen vendor-documented verbs: read account, links, QR codes and analytics for each object; create a link with a custom address, title and tags; update, archive, restore, pause and resume links; archive and restore QR codes. Containment is documented rather than implied: per-connector permission approval with individual scopes untickable on the consent screen, an email on every connection, immediate revocation, no permanent delete anywhere, and no route to API keys, plan, billing or account settings from an assistant. Held to `★★` rather than `★★★`: the retention window, the bot filtering and the click-to-unique-visitor question are not published on the pages read, so a click count is not a visitor count, and new links consume a monthly plan limit.
- [App Store Connect MCP - Sales, Proceeds, Reviews and Releases From Apple's Own API](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/app-store-connect-mcp/) · local stdio Go binary, MIT, `brew install idoo/tap/app-store-connect-mcp` with the tap answering 200, Docker image and `.mcpb` bundle, registry `io.github.idoo/app-store-connect-mcp` at 0.13.0, by Ivan Verevkin (github.com/idoo). No endpoint to probe, so the evidence is the repository's **generated tool reference**: **76 tools**, each tagged read, write or destructive, with a confirm mode of `none`, `flag`, `plan` or `human`, across sixteen toolsets of which six are on by default. The revenue side is the reason to catalogue it: `sales_report` returns Sales and Trends aggregates - units by category, proceeds per currency, top-N, with `include_rows` giving a CSV link - for a period from `from`/`to` or `frequency` plus `report_date`; `analytics_report` sums an app's newest analytics segments by dimension on a 24 to 48 hour lag; `analytics_setup` is the prerequisite that creates the ONGOING report request; `insights_summary` answers "how is my app doing" in one call with units and proceeds against the previous period plus ratings, versions and TestFlight feedback, each section marked ok or unavailable with the reason; and `analytics_funnel_report` walks impressions to page views to downloads with conversion by source and territory, sessions, crashes, installs against deletions and a previous-period comparison. Releases are a workflow rather than a bag of REST calls: `release_status` preflights a version, `release_prepare` applies a `plan_id`, `release_submit` submits the version with IAPs and subscriptions, `release_publish` releases, `release_phased` drives a seven-day rollout and `release_cancel` empties a draft. Anything public or hard to undo is destructive class with a human gate through elicitation, raw API calls validate against a pinned spec before running, and `doctor` checks key, JWT, Apple reachability, clock skew, rate limit and write mode with a fix per finding. Limitations recorded: local stdio only so nothing was executed here, an App Store Connect API key per team is a real credential with account reach, analytics lags 24 to 48 hours and the funnel needs `analytics_setup` first, reviewer messages live only in the Resolution Center, and this is a young single-maintainer project at 1 star and version 0.13.0. This is the account-side complement to `AppSigma`, which reads the public store as a market rather than the account as a ledger.

## 🆕 October 26, 2026 - Midday Sweep (3 New, 3 Guides)

Seven hours after the morning pass the listing had not moved at all: 17,522 servers at the 13:32Z reader stamp, the same page-one order, and 119 slugs read across pages 1 to 4 with 58 of them fresh after the three-way classification. The feed page 1 would not render through the reader proxy this cycle, which served nothing but the sponsor rails, so the cards were read from the raw page with a browser user agent, 30 of them, and the newest card was already inside the morning dispositions. The delta came from the two surfaces that always move at this gap: the submission window, which filed twenty-two issues between #6155 and #6176 with no gaps, and the listing cards that were never dispositioned on any earlier ledger. Three entries earned guides, and each was driven rather than described: two answered without any key and one published its terms in its own 401.

- [POD Benchmark MCP - Print-on-Demand Supplier Costs](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/podbenchmark-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://podbenchmark.com/api/mcp`, **no auth at all**, read-only, 120 requests per minute per IP, official registry entry `com.podbenchmark/podbenchmark`, by POD Benchmark (podbenchmark.com). **Driven end to end without a key**: `initialize` returned HTTP 200 as `podbenchmark` 1.0.0 on protocol 2025-06-18 advertising tools and resources, `tools/list` returned **ten tools** with full JSON schemas, and two calls were executed against live data. `list_suppliers` returned seven suppliers with their vendor pages: Printful, Printify, Gelato, CustomCat, Prodigi, Inkthreadable and Fourthwall, the last two flagged `type: direct` rather than marketplace. `list_categories` returned `destination: US`, `currency: USD` and per-category counts with starting delivered prices: Apparel 1,971 products of which 1,722 carry a price across six suppliers from $11.33, T-Shirts 457 products with 389 priced from $12.08, Hoodies 277 products with 232 priced from $12.08. The rest of the surface is the comparison itself: `compare_product` takes a `canonicalProductId` with a destination and currency and returns which supplier is cheaper, `get_product_options` prices one product in a named size or colour, and `resolve_supplier_link` accepts a pasted supplier URL from any of the seven and returns the normalized product, which is the step that makes a like-for-like comparison possible without a shared product id. Limitations recorded: the normalization is the vendor's and a wrong merge produces a confident wrong comparison, one apparel product in eight has no price, other destinations and currencies are parameters rather than defaults, and tax, shipping terms and returns sit outside the server, so this compares cost and not landed obligation. Catalogued as a reversal of the August 26 hold on BestPrintOnDemand, which was held as a thin site-published comparison: the evidence that changes the disposition is ten live tools, keyless execution returning real supplier and category payloads, per-size and per-colour pricing and a supplier-link resolver across seven suppliers, which is a procurement surface rather than a price table.

- [GPU Finder MCP - Live Cloud GPU Prices and Stock](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/gpufinder-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://gpufinder.dev/mcp`, free API key as a Bearer token at 60 operations a month with `tools/list` readable without one, by GPU Finder (gpufinder.dev). **`initialize` returned HTTP 200 as `gpufinder` version `a6`** and `tools/list` returned **eight tools** keyless, so the capability is read from live schemas rather than from a listing: `list_gpus` carries VRAM, memory type, bandwidth, interconnect, provider and instance counts and min/max hourly price per model, `list_providers` carries each provider's GPU and instance counts, price range, **egress cost per GB and free egress allowance**, and last update time, `get_prices` returns every offer for one model and node size with region and on-demand against spot per whole node hour, `get_availability` returns day-by-day stock over seven days as instances observed available against total, `get_price_history` returns twelve UTC months per provider, `get_market_snapshot` answers the cheapest listed offer **and the cheapest offer actually observed in stock**, `get_data_status` reports collection freshness and each provider's last success, consecutive failures and last error, and `get_usage` reports allowance without spending it. A `tools/call` returned HTTP 401 `invalid_credential` that states the terms in the error rather than a signup wall: an API key is required, keys are free with 60 operations a month, created at the developers page and sent as a Bearer header. Vendor numbers at the probe: 33 providers, 24 availability APIs, 96 GPU models, data collected 43 minutes earlier, with 8x H100 quoted from $15.46/hr at Vast to $186.61/hr at Azure, a 12x spread, and a per-provider stale marker showing 30 hours since one provider's last successful refresh beside another marked out of stock. Limitations recorded: 60 operations a month is enough for periodic checks and not for hourly polling, tool execution was not driven because no key was created so argument names come from the published schemas, spot is not offered everywhere, storage and commitments are not modelled, and alerts are an email product outside MCP. Catalogued because it closes the gap left by the FastGPU hold, whose reason was an endpoint that could not be verified from public pages: this endpoint answers keyless on both handshake methods, and it answers the stock question that a price list alone does not.

- [ChargingNear.me MCP - US EV Charging Station Data](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/chargingnear-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://chargingnear.me/api/mcp`, **no auth at all**, free and read-only, data from the US Department of Energy station records under **CC-BY-4.0**, by ChargingNear.me. **Three calls executed keyless and the citation block returned on every response.** `initialize` returned HTTP 200 as `chargingnearme` v1.1.0 whose instructions are a constraint rather than marketing, read-only access to the directory and cite `citation_url` when you use a result. `tools/list` returned **six tools**: station search by city, state, network, connector, speed, minimum power or live availability, nearest stations to a coordinate, station detail by id, city stats, state stats and a corridor search around a route of waypoints. Executed: `get_city_charging_stats` with `scottsdale-az` returned **179 stations, 16 DC fast and 162 Level 2**, networks led by ChargePoint, Blink, Tesla Destination, non-networked and Tesla, a centroid and `updated_at: 2026-10-26T14:39:20.943Z`; `get_state_charging_stats` with `arizona` returned **1,760 stations across 100 cities, 232 DC fast and 1,465 Level 2** with ten networks named including Electrify America, eVgo and LOOP; `search_stations` for Scottsdale DC fast returned real site records with street address, zip, per-level port counts, `J1772COMBO` connector codes, access hours and a `citation_url`. The vendor states coverage of **95,724 stations across 64,285 locations and 289,475 ports**, refreshed daily from the DOE feed, exposed as REST, MCP, GeoJSON and a ChatGPT app. Limitations recorded: United States only, city and state tools require a slug so an unknown city fails on a required parameter rather than matching, the records inherit the government feed's own gaps including null pricing and one executed station reporting `max_power_kw: 3.70` beside a DC fast connector count, live availability is not a reservation, and CC-BY-4.0 makes attribution a licence condition on every downstream publication. Catalogued because charging density is a location variable a fleet, a retailer or a service business has to answer before committing, and because the citation URL travels with the answer.

## 🆕 October 26, 2026 - Morning Sweep (3 New, 3 Guides)

The listing that had been frozen through Sunday came back with a moderation batch, 17,360 to 17,522, and the same pass read 17,521 and 17,354 on later pages, which is one directory applying a batch mid-read rather than three directories. Eight pages and 240 cards were matched against the catalog on product names rather than registry slugs, because the registry derives URLs from domains. Three entries earned guides, each on a different kind of proof.

- [CitedBy MCP - Whether AI Assistants Can Find and Cite a Page](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/citedby-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://citedby.eu/mcp`, **no auth at all**, free and read-only, not listed in the official registry, by CitedBy (citedby.eu). **Driven end to end without a key**: `initialize` returned HTTP 200 as `citedby` 1.0.0 on protocol 2025-06-18, `tools/list` returned four tools in 2.9 KB of schema, and all four were executed against `corpusiq.io`. `check_ai_crawler_access` returned 8 of 8 crawlers can read the site dated `2026-10-26`, each line labelled with what that bot does: GPTBot for training, OAI-SearchBot for citing you in answers, ChatGPT-User for opening a page when a person asks, PerplexityBot for citing you, ClaudeBot for training, Google-Extended for Gemini grounding, and Bingbot and Googlebot for citing you. `check_llms_txt` returned `present: true`, 11,256 bytes, 10 links checked, 0 broken, and `/llms-full.txt` answering 200. `check_page` returned **score 90/100 with two findings**, `schema_rejected` because a `SoftwareApplication` block is missing `offers.price` or one of `aggregateRating` or `review`, and `render_blocking` at 0 scripts and 7 stylesheets, each finding carrying the consequence and the fix rather than a grade. `backlinks` returned `in_data: false` with the coverage window stated instead of a zero: 264,847 domains holding 100 or more referring domains under `.eu`, EU and UK country domains plus the most-linked sites, from the Common Crawl graph `cc-main-2026-aug-sep-oct` read on 2026-10-23. Limitations recorded: one page per call and a whole-site audit needs a plan, Common Crawl open data leaves most US small businesses outside coverage, robots.txt is respected so a blocked crawler returns that fact instead of a score, and the score measures structure rather than whether the writing answers a question. Catalogued because a blocked crawler is total invisibility that never appears as a traffic drop, and because this is the first checker on this beat that refuses to score what it could not read, beside `creavores-aeo-mcp` and the AI visibility entries.
- [Adspy MCP - Competitor Ad Creative Research in the Assistant](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/adspy-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://www.adspy.sh/mcp`, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and a client ID metadata document, paid from $19 a month, not listed in the official registry, by Adspy (adspy.sh). **Auth gated on `initialize`** with HTTP 401 `{"error":"Connect an authorized Adspy account.","code":"invalid_token"}`, so the capability is read from the server's own documents: the RFC 9728 protected resource returns `resource: https://www.adspy.sh/mcp`, one authorization server, header bearer tokens and five scopes, `read`, `write`, `discovery`, `export` and `usage`, with `resource_name: Adspy creative research`; the authorization server metadata names authorize, token, revoke and register endpoints, `response_types_supported: ["code"]`, authorization code and refresh grants, PKCE `S256`, `token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported: ["none"]` and `client_id_metadata_document_supported: true`. Per the vendor listing the library holds over two million creatives from 2,000+ advertisers across Meta and Google with organic TikTok, YouTube and Instagram posts on the paid tiers, and every result returns the hook, angle, format, call to action and a transcript, with collections and notes for a team, and a creative traceable to the same post later run as an ad. Plans are $19 Starter on one source with 2,000 credits, $39 Pro on every source with 6,000, $99 Unlimited with no credit count, and Enterprise adding a REST API, with the credit conversion published as roughly 22, 66 or unlimited Brand Full Analyses a month and extra users at +$5, +$15 and +$29. Limitations recorded: no spend and no ROAS ever, no ad account connected, no free tier, and the tool schemas were not read because discovery needs a session. Catalogued because it reads public advertising rather than an account, so a business with no relationship to a competitor still gets the material, beside `openadlibrary-mcp` for the same data read twice and `paidsync-mcp` and `adrails-mcp` for the execution leg.
- [GBPly MCP - Google Business Profile With Approval Gates](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/gbply-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://mcp.gbply.net/v1`, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and no API key, included with a GBPly account, not listed in the official registry, by GBPly (gbply.net). Gated on both `initialize` and `tools/list` with HTTP 401 `{"error":"unauthorized"}`. **The finding is in the discovery documents**: the `WWW-Authenticate` header points at `https://mcp.gbply.net/functions/v1/mcp/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, which answers `{"error":"not_found","use":"https://mcp.gbply.net/v1"}`, while the live document at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` returns `resource: https://mcp.gbply.net/v1`, an authorization server at `https://mcp.gbply.net/oauth`, header bearer tokens and **no `scopes_supported` field at all**, and that server's metadata returns `scopes_supported: ["email","profile","offline_access"]` with PKCE `S256` and `response_types_supported: ["code"]`. Identity scopes only, no `reviews:write` and no `posts:write`: authorization over business data lives in the product's request system rather than in the token, the opposite of the eight resource scopes `Leadpages MCP` publishes. Capability from the vendor connector documentation: read on workspaces, profiles, completeness, insights running 2-3 days behind, monthly search terms, reviews and rating stats, posts, photos, Q&A, Profile Guard changes, Rank Tracker and citation scans, analysis reports and credit balances; draft with nothing saved for AI review replies, Q&A suggestions and rank-scan cost previews; a request for every publish, schedule, edit or delete of a reply or post, every saved FAQ, every profile field, every Profile Guard decision and every paid scan; and direct only for a Google sync a few times an hour. **Requests expire in fifteen minutes and run once**, and on approval the vendor re-checks permission, credits, plan limits and the daily post cap, keeping a post that fails policy as flagged rather than published. An optional per-action Always allow covers publish, profile change, spend credits with a most-per-request and a most-per-24-hours limit, and deletes of things not yet live, scoped to one assistant in one workspace, overridable by the workspace owner and only switchable from a 2FA sign-in in a 2FA workspace, with every auto-approved action labelled as such. Permissions are inherited, so a viewer can read and draft but cannot create requests, staff and admin features are never reachable through the connector, and demo profiles are read-only. One of them answers without a key, and it does arithmetic no other entry in this catalog performs.

- [RevClamp MCP - Stripe Revenue Leakage and Chargeback Proof](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/revclamp-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://api.revclamp.com/api/mcp`, no OAuth (the protected resource document returns 404, so the connection is a workspace key in the client config rather than a consent flow), registry `io.github.revclamp/revclamp-mcp` active since `2026-10-25T02:54:03Z`, manifest at `https://revclamp.com/.well-known/mcp.json` naming npm `revclamp-mcp` 1.20.6 and a pinned tarball SHA-256, by RevClamp Enterprise (revclamp.com). **Driven end to end without a key**: unauthenticated `initialize` returned HTTP 200 as `revclamp-mcp` 1.20.6 on protocol 2025-06-18, `tools/list` returned nine tools, and seven were executed with real arguments. A 250,000 cent wholesale order paid at 75,000 on Net-30 returned `state: DEPOSIT_CLEARED_ACTIVE`, `requiredDepositCents: 75000`, `remainingBalanceCents: 175000`, `releaseHoldAction: true` and the tag `b2b_net_terms:deposit_cleared`; a dispute payload returned `utf16CodeUnits: 19113` against `maxUtf16Ceiling: 18000`, `withinCeiling: false`, `overallVerdict: FAIL_UTF16_OVERFLOW` while the CE 3.0 rubric itself passed with two prior matches and both IP and device matching, which is the failure that kills an otherwise perfect answer; a Stripe style HMAC verified as `signatureValid: true` with `timingSafeCompared: true` and a 300 second tolerance, and the same call with a wrong `v1` returned `HMAC_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH`; the replay simulator dropped two copies of an expired event and reported `naiveHandlerBug: APPLIED_EXPIRED_REPLAY_OUTSIDE_72H_WINDOW` against `naiveFinalTier: growth_59`, naming the free paid tier a naive webhook handler would have granted; `GR123456789` normalised to `EL123456789` and returned `FORMAT_VALID_UNVERIFIED` with `zeroRateAllowed: false` rather than a green light; and a past due subscription 40 days past its invoice failure returned `isGhostLeak: true` with `UNPAID_GHOST_USAGE_CONFIRMED`. Zero trust guard found in the same session: any argument that looks like a live secret is refused with `-32602 LIVE_SECRET_FORBIDDEN_IN_SANDBOX`, so a production webhook secret never travels through the chat. Limitations recorded rather than smoothed over: it is not a Stripe connector, since the tools take billing objects as arguments or read telemetry forwarded to `POST /v1/events/ingest` and nothing lists customers, invoices or revenue; dispute staging is `submit: false` by design with no mutation of any external system; every VIES mode except `LIVE` is a deterministic simulation, kept deliberately to rehearse the HTTP 200 soft failure the Commission's service actually produces; scope is B2B net terms in euro cents with no other currency or billing platform; and no tool call to `stage_stripe_dispute_ce3` was attempted because it needs a live dispute shape across four nested objects. Free tier $0 with 5,000 events and all nine tools, then $19, $59 and $199 a month at 100,000, 1,000,000 and 5,000,000 events, flat rate with a stated 0 percent dispute commission against the 25 to 30 percent contingency an agency charges. Catalogued for the three records nothing else here measures: unpaid usage on a subscription that is still live, dispute evidence against the network rubric rather than against an opinion, and a wholesale order against its deposit gate, beside `paidnice-mcp` for receivables after the invoice and `honest-vies-mcp` for VAT number validation.

Pass an Apify API token in the Authorization: Bearer header."}`, so the drivable path was the MIT repository, cloned and built locally: `npm install`, `npm run build`, `PORT=3311 node dist/http.js`, `initialize` returning HTTP 200 with `serverInfo` `shoptrueprofit-fee-mcp` 1.0.0 on protocol 2025-06-18, `tools/list` returning all 13. Five real calls: `ebay_profit` at `price 25`, `shipping_charged 5`, `item_cost 8`, `shipping_label_cost 4`, `promoted_listings_pct 5` returned "eBay profit $12.02 on $30.00 revenue (40.07% margin) after $5.98 fees and $12.00 costs. Break-even price $10.24 per unit" with the final value fee line stating "13.6% on the portion up to $7,500; 2.35% on the portion over $7,500 (per item, on the total amount of the sale incl. shipping and tax)", the per-order fee $0.40 on "order total $30.00 > $10" and promoted listings $1.50 at "5% of $30.00"; `etsy_fees` at `price 24.99`, `shipping_charged 5`, `offsite_ads_pct 15`, `region us` returned "$7.80 (26% of revenue)" from listing $0.20, transaction $1.95 at 6.5%, processing $1.15 at "3% of $29.99 + 0.25 USD" and Offsite Ads $4.50 at "15% of $29.99, max 100 per order"; `amazon_fees` at `price 29.99`, `category home-kitchen`, `fulfillment fba`, 10 x 8 x 4 inches, 1.5 lb, `ship_date 2026-11-20` returned "$11.66 (38.89% of revenue)" with referral $4.50 at 15% and a $0.30 minimum, FBA fulfilment $6.49 priced on "Large standard, 2.3 lb shipping weight, peak standard card" (dimensional weight beating the 1.5 lb entered, since 10 x 8 x 4 inches is 320 cubic inches) and a $0.23 fuel and logistics surcharge that appears only inside the October 15 to January 14 peak window; `compare_marketplaces` at `price 34.99`, `item_cost 9`, `shipping_label_cost 4.5`, `shipping_charged 5`, `target_margin_pct 30` returned Etsy $22.24 profit at 55.62%, eBay $20.65 at 51.64% and Amazon FBA $13.58 at 38.8%, with Amazon revenue at $34.99 rather than $39.99 because FBA shipping is set by Amazon and the buyer's $5 never arrives; `amazon_target_price` at `category home-kitchen`, `fulfillment fba`, `target_margin_pct 30`, `item_cost 9` returned "list at $29.39 for a 30% margin; break-even $19.02", solved rather than divided because the referral percentage and the fulfilment band both move with the price. Free reference lookups returned `count: 11` eBay final-value-fee categories, `count: 37` Amazon referral categories and `count: 12` Etsy Payments regions. Every response carries a dated fee table (`ebay-us-2026-10-16`, `amazon-us-2026-10-16`, `etsy-2026-10-13`), the engine file and its `engine_sha256`, the assumptions applied, official source URLs and a `calculator_url` for the seller-facing page the same engine drives. **Catalog gap closed:** the catalog carried marketplace listings, orders and ad spend, and nothing that priced the marketplace itself - take-rate is the largest missing cost line in the e-commerce group. **Gap named rather than claimed:** the vendor's 1,700+ case cross-check against Amazon's and eBay's own worked examples is not reproducible from a public clone because those tests need the private app source and skip themselves - `npm test` returned 94 passed and 31 skipped, the whole `crosscheck.test.ts` file among the skips, which the README states outright rather than letting a green run imply otherwise. **Limitations recorded rather than smoothed over:** US-only marketplace scope (eBay.com US, Amazon.com US, Etsy's 12 payment regions for processing rates), a named list of fee programmes deliberately not modelled (eBay Store subscriptions; Etsy Ads cost-per-click, Etsy Plus, currency conversion and the Regulatory Operating Fee; Amazon's low-inventory, inbound-placement, returns-processing, aged-inventory and storage-utilisation surcharges, lithium battery fees, removal and disposal, the Overmax handling fee, and FBA rates after January 14 2027 falling back to 2026 non-peak rates with a warning), estimates rather than settlement statements, and a repository created `2026-10-17` with 0 stars whose track record does not yet match its engineering.

- [Adrails MCP - Ad Spend Reconciled to Real Revenue](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/adrails-mcp/) · remote server at `https://adrails.ai/api/mcp`, Streamable HTTP with OAuth 2.1, by TBSS Labs, LLC (adrails.ai). Live probe: unauthenticated `POST initialize` returned HTTP 401 with `www-authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://adrails.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"` and the body `{"error":"invalid_token","message":"Connect to Adrails to continue."}`; that document returned 200 with resource `https://adrails.ai/api/mcp`, authorization server `https://adrails.ai/api/auth`, `bearer_methods_supported: ["header"]` and six scopes (`adrails:read`, `adrails:actions:prepare`, `adrails:integrations:manage`, `adrails:workflows:manage`, `adrails:knowledge:write`, `adrails:campaigns:write`), and the vendor server card at `/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json` returned protocol 2025-11-25 with `serverInfo` Adrails 1.0.0 and the tools capability. Tools: 69 published, 49 of them the agent's own and 20 for accounts, integrations, campaign drafts, automations, Knowledge and job status, each documenting its inputs, its per-operation permission, the role it needs and its error contract, with `tools/list` returning only what the connection's permissions and the caller's role allow. Three access shapes are declared per tool: read, change (acts at once and needs an idempotency key) and proposal for approval. A proposal returns `status: awaiting_approval`, an `actionId`, a field-by-field preview, an `expiresAt` and a link at `adrails.ai/oauth/actions/<actionId>`; any current owner or admin of the workspace approves it signed in as themselves, Adrails re-reads the platform and applies the exact change once or blocks it if the entity moved, and the proposal expires 24 hours after it was prepared (30 minutes in-app). Budget changes cap at 30% each, an increase needs measured spend and results, bulk selection covers at most 40 entities, and everything Adrails creates starts paused. Idempotency is enforced rather than advisory, errors return as tool results with `isError` so the model can correct the call, a result over 256,000 bytes is refused whole with no partial figures, and limits run 60 calls a minute per token, 10 changes a minute, 180 a minute per person and 600 per workspace. Business sources read beside ad spend: Shopify, Stripe, Klaviyo, Triple Whale, PostHog, RevenueCat and Google Drive. Two tools carry the entry. `store_revenue` returns gross, refunded and net sales kept apart, in each store's own currency, never converted. `business_review` accepts an explanation only when every number quotes its source word for word, from the person's own statement or from a tool result in the connection's history, which is a provenance rule enforced inside the tool rather than a disclaimer beside it. `budget_recommend` compares the latest two complete seven-day windows in the account's time zone and suggests no amount. Plans from the vendor's own page: Preview free with 10 credits once, Starter $49 a month with 200 credits, Growth $149 with 700, Scale $399 with 2,000, unlimited ad accounts and team members on every paid plan, every connector included, no percentage of ad spend, and MCP tool calls at zero credits. **Gap named rather than claimed:** no tool call was made, because every tool needs an OAuth connection to a workspace with a connected ad account, so the entry rests on the live 401, the protected-resource metadata, the server card and the vendor's 69-tool reference.

- [UniPost MCP - LinkedIn and X Publishing With Approval](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/unipost-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP server at `https://mcp.unipost.ai/mcp`, OAuth in the browser or a workspace API key, by UniPost (unipost.ai). Live probe: unauthenticated `POST initialize` returned HTTP 401 carrying the server's own message, `{"error":{"code":-32001,"message":"Sign in to UniPost, or create an API key in UniPost → API keys."}}`. Seven tools are named in the vendor's reference: `list_accounts`, `list_posts`, `schedule_post`, `approve_post`, `cancel_post`, `get_analytics` and `get_x_allowance`. Scheduling and approving are separate tools on purpose, `schedule_post` always creates `pending_approval` and returns an approval link, a post created by another person's agent cannot be approved through the tool at all, and TikTok posts must be approved on the vendor screen because their privacy settings live there. Pricing is graduated per connected account, two free, $3 for accounts 3 to 10, $1 for 11 to 30 and $0.50 above, yearly at ten times monthly. The X credit model is the operationally load-bearing fact: a plain post costs 1 credit, a post containing a link costs 13, the free allowance is 10 credits a month, and a paid workspace gets 50 per X account for its first ten and 20 after, with 10 posts an hour and 25 a day enforced at publish time rather than at schedule time. **Packaged addition, not a gap:** the publishing class is six deep here through PendPost, TimeToPost, BulkPublish, Blog2Social, Chirpie and Maeve Social, and this is recorded for the pricing shape and the two-tool approval split.

Eight tools: `create_project`, `check_bom`, `update_bom_line`, `find_parts`, `get_part`, `find_alternatives`, `place_order`, `order_status`. The surface is a bill of materials priced for a real build: 630,000+ in-stock parts from the JLCPCB/LCSC library refreshed daily, with DigiKey and Mouser checked live on every line so prices and stock sit side by side, plus manufacturer lifecycle warnings for parts that are not recommended for new designs or are end of life. `check_bom` returns per-distributor price comparison, the shipments with estimated shipping and a `quote_id`, and flags rather than repairs: out of stock, not enough stock, uncertain matches, an MPN and a distributor number on one line pointing at different parts, a missing footprint, and the JLCPCB extended-part fee when assembly is requested. `update_bom_line` re-prices the whole build after a swap, so accepting an alternative is one call and one new quote. `place_order` requests an order and charges nothing; the team re-checks live stock and price and emails a payment link. Positions are never interpolated, suspicious jumps are flagged rather than deleted, each response carries the source attribution its licence requires (Digitraffic under CC BY 4.0 among them), and private vessels are never listed individually on any plan. ## 🆕 October 21, 2026 - Night Sweep (4 New, 4 Guides)

Night delta about six hours after the evening capture, and for the first time this week the three discovery surfaces disagreed with each other: the mcp.so `/feed` page 1 returned 30 cards with six posted inside the window, mcpservers.org `/all` pages 1 to 4 returned 120 cards with page 4 run for the first time (both earlier passes recorded it as not run), and the chatmcp/mcpso issue window that the last two passes also recorded as not run had 43 submissions behind it, #5817 through #5861. Four business-relevant entries, each with a guide, and three of the four were settled by running the endpoint rather than by reading a listing.

- [Tenantback MCP - CAM Reconciliation Audit](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/tenantback-mcp/) · remote server at `https://tenantback.com/mcp`, no key needed for audits, A2A endpoint alongside it, by Tenantback (tenantback.com). Live probe: unauthenticated `POST initialize` returned HTTP 200 (serverInfo `tenantback` 1.0.0 on protocol 2025-06-18) and `tools/list` returned `audit_cam_reconciliation` and `get_audit_result`. A workspace key adds nine more: `portfolio_overview`, `list_locations`, `get_lease_abstract`, `search_lease_documents`, `list_findings`, `list_deadlines`, `get_statement`, `request_audit`, `get_audit_request`, `draft_dispute` (drafts only, a person approves sending). The audit checks pro-rata share and its denominator, CAM caps cumulative and non-cumulative, admin and management fee rate and base, excluded costs, gross-up above the occupancy threshold, year-over-year variance, the balance due and late statement delivery. The lease quote is verified against the source page and the arithmetic is computed in code, so a finding either balances against the statement line or it does not. Free audits are capped at 5 per sender a day with 10 files per request and 20 MB per file; recovery work is 25% of money actually recovered, and the portfolio plan is $49 per location a month plus 12% of recoveries. **Catalog gap closed:** every commercial-property entry here concerns managing an asset (Hercules Property, Dutch Property Context, AskRent, LucidRents); none audited the expense reconciliation a tenant is billed for.

## 🆕 October 20, 2026 - Evening Sweep (7 Servers, 1 Guide)

Evening delta about seven hours after the midday capture. The mcp.so `/feed` page 1 returned 30 cards and mcpservers.org `/all` pages 1 to 3 about 90, and one vendor produced the whole cycle: Copliancy Inc published seven product servers inside a single hour, all for the same customer, and together they close a gap this catalog has carried since it began tracking operations software.

- [Copliancy MCP Suite - Licenses, Leases and Incidents per Location](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/copliancy-mcp/) · seven remote servers from Copliancy Inc (copliancy.com), a US multi-location compliance and record platform used across hospitality, grocery, healthcare, oil and gas, transport, education and construction. **IncidentVault** at `https://app.incidentvault.com/api/mcp/apps/server` covers incidents, claims, reserves, settlements, legal spend, risk checks, regulatory inspections and tasks in 38 scopes (19 read, 19 write, plus `offline_access`); its protected-resource document sets `bearer_methods_supported: ["header"]` and its authorization server publishes authorize, token, registration and revocation endpoints for PKCE S256 with dynamic client registration. **PolicyTrak** at `https://app.policytrak.com/api/mcp` covers sites, compliance fields, policies, SOPs, laws, acknowledgements, workflows, files, audit trails and imports across 57 scopes. **RetailHardHat** at `https://app.retailhardhat.com/api/mcp` runs site development from due diligence through permits, bids, RFIs, project budgets, change requests and invoices to opening day in 20 scopes. **CredentialCamp** at `https://app.credentialcamp.com/api/mcp` tracks credentials, certifications and mandated training in 5. **QuipAssist** at `https://app.quipassist.com/api/mcp` is the maintenance layer - equipment, work orders, preventive schedules, parts, vendors, IoT readings - in 13 scopes, one of them `documents:sensitive`. **LeaseCommand** at `https://app.leasecommand.com/api/mcp` carries leases, rent schedules, critical dates and ASC 842 amortization with journal entries. **SmartShifts** at `https://app.smartshifts.com/api/mcp/apps/server` covers shifts, coverage, time off and tasks. Verified live this sweep: all seven endpoints answered a `POST initialize` probe with 401 or 403 and never a 200 without credentials; five publish OAuth protected-resource metadata, SmartShifts returns 404 on that path and LeaseCommand serves its application HTML there, so both are described as declaring scopes without publishing metadata. The design worth reading: every call checks the user's role, location and record limits, so an agent handed to a store manager cannot enumerate another store. IncidentVault documents two surfaces and the difference between them - the operational endpoint returns opaque record IDs, allowlisted status and priority, dates, location IDs and audit percentages while excluding names, narratives, medical details, custom fields and attachments, and the private endpoint keeps the full authorized catalog. Writes are opt-in and every modifying tool produces a saved preview a person approves inside the product; the vendor is explicit that pending or approved is not executed success. MCP Apps hosts render a working dashboard; other hosts get structured facts and source links, and Gemini widget support is not assumed. Free sign-up, tier pricing not published in text. **Catalog gap closed:** A4B, ZenSched and STEADYWRK cover assets, workforce scheduling and field dispatch as single-purpose tools, and nothing here carried license and permit renewals, incident and claims records, ASC 842 lease accounting or credential compliance across locations.

**Also identified this cycle (not catalogued):** on the mcp.so feed window, read and held: superbot (a name and a URL, no statement of what data it reads), Mr BnB Santiago (single-city travel vertical), Health by Dr Brad (consumer health plan builder), Housecall Pro assistant (browser automation over a field-service product rather than a data interface), KissCode, OC Maker, DolphinRadar, Vectoree, Paprika3d and Volley.sh (consumer, creator and developer utilities), Workspace369 (client-work suite whose classes are carried by the catalogued professional-services and invoicing entries), SCDO Agent Ledger (agent payment infrastructure), Organize with AI (personal media management) and FrontRowTickets (single-vertical inventory). On mcpservers.org pages 2 and 3, the new cards: NotebookLM MCP by useapi.net held because it is a third-party paid wrapper at $15 a month that acts on your own Google account; tropia.pl held and recorded for a revisit since it carries board members, shareholders, financial statements and public contracts for the Polish KRS registry and this catalog holds UK, US and multi-country registries but nothing for Poland; Shipday held because the listing points at documentation hosted as an S3 PDF with no verifiable tool list; upcoach held as a narrow coaching-program surface; Hazelchat and BubblaV held as thin website chatbot analytics; MailBeast against the outreach class; Pear against email, calendar and contacts; DomainRef as developer and ops hygiene; NeuralVerge against the aggregator class at 342 tools; Dutify against Taskade and Atwork; anakinio as scraping infrastructure; Timbré on the print-and-post precedent set by MailStream; LLMSlim against a dense memory class; PedalBro, LFG Alarm, EINI, Voidless, Arquimedes, Labreador, RobotBase, ScBee, KIRUPA, lakeboard-converter and Agent Payment Node as consumer, scientific or developer utilities. Carried dispositions from today's earlier captures were not re-litigated.

- [Azquo MCP - Audited Shared Memory for AI Agents](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/azquo-mcp/) · remote server at `https://data.azquo.ai/mcp`, official (azquo.com), OAuth 2.1 bearer with scope `mcp` or an API key from the Azquo admin site. Live probe: `initialize` returned HTTP 401 `Unauthorized : no key` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://data.azquo.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"`, and that metadata document returns resource `https://data.azquo.ai/mcp`, authorization server `https://data.azquo.ai`, `bearer_methods_supported: ["header"]`, `scopes_supported: ["mcp"]`, `resource_name: "Azquo"`. The capability list is the vendor's own wording because no `tools/list` is reachable without a credential: create databases, import raw files, design and refine import templates, query in AQL, browse and extend hierarchies, build and run reports, and audit any single figure back through every transformation to its source file, user and date, plus rehearse a risky change on a copy, see the history of a name, restore a deleted one and read every earlier value with who changed it and where it came from. The architecture is the reason it earns the entry: names in hierarchies rather than rows in tables, so a new dimension is a new lens over existing data instead of a migration, and provenance is per cell rather than per row. Multi-agent by design, with every write attributed to the agent and the person behind it, and the conventions an agent agrees are stored in the database where the next agent is told to read them. Backups are a plain file, stated to be readable without Azquo. Evaluation access is on request; no price is published, so cost is unverified.

Installed into a clean virtual environment and run in this sweep: `initialize` returned serverInfo `mcp-glp-audit-proxy 0.1.0` on protocol 2025-06-18 and wrote `audit/startup`, `initialize`, `notifications/initialized` and `tools/list` as eleven RFC 8785 canonical-JSON entries with SHA-256 `entry_hash` and `prev_hash` chaining; `glp_verify_chain` returned `chain ok entries=11 head=6669451c...`; the `mcp-glp-audit-proxy-verify` CLI returned `chain ok entries=12 shown=12` plus a per-entry listing with seq, time, record class, status, principal, role and method. The role model was verified by running two sessions against one config: an operator with no upstreams gets `tools: []`, while `qa` gets exactly three trail tools (`glp_verify_chain`, `glp_search_audit`, `glp_export_audit`). Policy: shell-glob allow and deny lists on the exposed `server__tool` name with deny winning and an empty allow list denying everything, roles `operator`/`approver`/`qa`/`admin`, reasons required for writes, single-use time-boxed approval bound to the SHA-256 of the canonical call, fail-closed append, and auditing that cannot be switched off (`audit_enabled: false` is denied and logged). Coverage is mapped clause by clause to OECD GLP No. 17, FDA 21 CFR Part 11 11.10(e), EU GMP Annex 11, MHRA and PIC/S PI 041-1, WHO TRS 1033 ALCOA+ and EU AI Act Articles 12 and 19. Stated limits: the community approval is not an electronic signature, WORM storage and signing are Pro, stdio only in 0.1.0, and the `.head` sidecar is not a defence against someone who can edit the log and the sidecar together.

Evening delta about eight and a half hours after the midday capture, and both directories rotated hard in the window: the mcp.so `/feed` page 1 (29 server and client links, six of them posted after the 19:30 UTC midday pull) plus mcpservers.org `/all` pages 1-4 through the r.jina.ai reader proxy (120 cards, 99 of them not named anywhere in the midday sweep or the night sweep before it). The six fresh feed cards were all consumer or developer utilities and were held. One new business-relevant entry, catalogued with a guide: a pre-action mandate gate for agent payments, verified rule by rule against its live endpoint.

- [drift MCP - Pre-Action Mandate Enforcement for AI Agents](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/drift-mcp/) · remote Streamable HTTP at `https://drift.rta.lat/mcp` (JSON-RPC 2.0, protocol 2025-06-18, server `drift 0.1.0`, no auth), Apache-2.0, `github.com/mrpkk/drift` at default branch `master`, created October 4, 2026, Python 3.11+, zero dependencies: the missing check between an agent being granted a payment mandate and the money leaving. AP2 verifies the mandate once at signature time and then steps away; drift re-checks six rules in a fixed order before every action - `amount`, `payee`, `audience`, `currency`, `window`, `intent` - with DENY as the default and the refusal naming the most important rule rather than an incidental one. Three tools, all annotated read-only and idempotent: `drift_check` (one action), `drift_session` (a batch, with per-action verdicts and a chain fingerprint that breaks if any earlier decision is rewritten or reordered) and `drift_explain` (the rules in order, with plain-language reasons). The mandate is a frozen dataclass, so an edit builds a new mandate instead of quietly widening the signed one; amounts are integer minor units; validity bounds are inclusive. Every rule was fired deliberately against the live endpoint - ALLOW within limits, then DENY `amount`, `payee`, `audience`, `currency`, `window` and `intent` from six separate probes, plus a three-action batch returning `{submitted: 3, allowed: 1, denied: 2, breach_by_rule: {"amount": 1, "payee": 1}}`. One footgun documented: an empty `allowed_intents` disables the intent rule and returned ALLOW for an intent named `transfer_everything`. Stated limits, from the vendor, are honest ones: it does not verify signatures (AP2's job), does not execute, keeps no state, and `intent` arrives as untrusted input from the agent; proving what actually happened is the same author's `attest`. **Install trap, verified:** the README says `pip install drift`, but PyPI `drift` is an unrelated CMS package at 0.0.7 and `drift-mcp` returns 404 - install from a clone with `pip install -e .`. Hosted free tier is 100 checks a day, then x402 per call on Base; self-hosting is free.

- [PhilForms MCP - Philippine Government Forms Filled into Sealed PDFs](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/philforms-mcp/) · local stdio client `npx -y github:philforms/philforms-mcp` (Node 18+, no dependencies, MIT) in front of the PhilForms HTTPS API (`https://philforms.com`, OpenAPI 3.1, api version 1.0.0, live: `openapi.json` returns 200 and states 1,342 forms): search and fill official Philippine government forms across BIR, SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, GSIS, COA, CSC and GPPB with every input mapped to its printed box, so a TIN lands digit by digit in its cells. Five tools - `search_forms`, `get_form_parameters` (the fill contract: every parameter, label, type, format and choice), `check_form_values` (validate before filling, rendered as it would print), `fill_form` (PDF plus tamper-evident document id), `verify_pdf` - over a wider documented API with dossier, ingest, scan and extraction endpoints and a verification ledger. Pricing is published in PHP by the plans endpoint (`/api/v1/plans`, 200): a free watermarked tier that still issues clean first-of-pack forms plus 5 clean 2307s a quarter and 5 clean 2316s a year, 500 test fills on a `pk_test_` key, credits where fill costs 1 and check, preview and verify cost 0 (revise 0 within 7 days, at most 5 edits), and form packs at 79 PHP for one form and 299 PHP for five, valid 12 months. The endpoint reported `is_checkout_available: false` at probe time, so the schedule is confirmed and the purchase path is not. Fills and prints; **you file** - not affiliated with any agency.

## 🆕 October 19, 2026 - Night Sweep (1 New, 1 Guide)

- [ACMP MCP - On-Prem IT Management with Approval Gate](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/acmp-mcp/) · self-hosted Streamable HTTP on your own ACMP server at `http://<HOST>:8765/` (JSON-RPC 2.0, protocol 2025-06-18; one personal API key per operator, optionally bound to that person's real ACMP identity): the Aagon ACMP client and asset management platform exposed as 118 tools across ten areas - clients and inventory (OS, last logged-on user, hardware, offline machines, agent versions, low disk space), software and security (installed software and search, outdated software, missing and failed Windows updates, CVEs with score and last scan time, Defender health, BitLocker state, licence over- and under-deployment), jobs and execution (`acmp_run_powershell` as SYSTEM), client commands and kiosk writers (optional, off by default), containers, assets and master data including contracts expiring soon, 18 helpdesk tools (read, create, update, close, reopen, comment, work time, costs), and TeamViewer support links - plus `acmp_call` over all 167 Public API commands. The approval gate is the design centre: reads run immediately, a write freezes as a request showing the plain-text PowerShell, the requester and the target machine, and runs only after one named approver agrees; execute and delete need two different approvers. Approval happens in a browser outside the model, and approver tokens are independent of the API keys. MIT; requires ACMP 6.9/6.10 with AESB/SICS and the Public API on Windows Server with .NET Framework 4.8; documentation is in German. Repository `github.com/Herzog-GmbH/acmp-mcp` created October 11, 2026 with release `mcpb-v1.0.0` (Claude Desktop extension) on October 18, 2026. Not probed by endpoint: the server runs behind the customer's own firewall, so there is no public URL to initialize against.

- [Hypotize MCP - Growth Experiment Memory for Agents](/hermes/mcp/servers/external/hypotize-mcp/) · hosted Streamable HTTP at `https://api.hypotize.ai/mcp` (OAuth 2.1; you sign in and choose what the agent may do): a shared experiment memory for teams and their agents - 21 tools over a project's tested backlog, framework-scored ideas (ICE, PIE, RICE or a custom framework), an enforced lifecycle with no skipped stages, and outcomes, evidence and learnings recorded together. Seven tools read the record (projects, project context and writing language, the backlog and pipeline, one experiment with its score and latest comments, learnings, tags and custom frameworks), twelve update it (create and update projects, import a backlog in all-or-nothing batches of 50, create ideas with variants, update experiments without overwriting newer work, record a vote and recalculate priority, transition stages, record the outcome with learning and evidence, add dated comments, set the action plan, create tags and frameworks) and two delete records, off until you grant the delete scope at connection. It keeps the record, not the test runner - Hypotize does not run A/B tests or assign traffic. Ships with three skills (growth experiments, weekly review, backlog import); works with Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, Kimi, OpenClaw, Hermes and any MCP client. Publisher: Hypotize (hypotize.ai; plugin repo github.com/viluca94/hypotize-plugin). Live probe: POST initialize to `api.hypotize.ai/mcp` returns 401 UNAUTHORIZED; `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` returns 200 naming the resource, the `hypotize:read` / `hypotize:write` / `hypotize:delete` scopes and `offline_access`, and `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` names the authorize, token, revoke and dynamic-registration endpoints.
